question.name: Question 6
question.problem:
A company manufactures electronic components. Of the components manufactured, $45%$ are produced by the first machine, $25%$ are produced by the second machine, and the third machine produces the remaining.
If $8%$ of the components produced by the first machine, $4%$ produced by the second machine, and $5%$ produced by the third machine are defective, what is the probability that a randomly selected component is defective?
question.worked_solution:
Let $D$ be the event that a randomly selected component is defective, and 

- let ${B}_{1}$ be the event that the component was produced by the first machine,

- let ${B}_{2}$ be the event that the component was produced by the second machine,

- let ${B}_{3}$ be the event that the component was produced by the third machine.

Then the disjoint union ${B}_{1}⊔{B}_{2}⊔{B}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected component is defective, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D\cap {B}_{1})+P(D\cap {B}_{2})+P(D\cap {B}_{3}) \\  & =P(D|{B}_{1})P({B}_{1})+P(D|{B}_{2})P({B}_{2})+P(D|{B}_{3})P({B}_{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since the first machine produces $45%$ of the components, the second machine produces $25%$ of the components, the third machine produces the remaining

$$
100%-(45%+25%)=30%.
$$

As a result, we have

$$
P({B}_{1})=0.45,\,P({B}_{2})=0.25,\,P({B}_{3})=0.3.
$$

- Since $8%$ of the components produced by the first machine, $4%$ produced by the second machine, and $5%$ produced by the third machine are defective, we have

$$
P(D|{B}_{1})=0.08,\,P(D|{B}_{2})=0.04,\,P(D|{B}_{3})=0.05.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected component is defective is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D|{B}_{1})P({B}_{1})+P(D|{B}_{2})P({B}_{2})+P(D|{B}_{3})P({B}_{3}) \\  & =(0.08)(0.45)+(0.04)(0.25)+(0.05)(0.3) \\  & =0.036+0.01+0.015 \\  & =0.061.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 7
question.problem: A company manufactures three types of cars. Of the car population, $40%$ are model ${C}_{1},$  $35%$ are model ${C}_{2},$ and the remaining cars are model ${C}_{3}.$ If $6%$ of the model ${C}_{1},$ $4%$ of the model  ${C}_{2},$ and $2%$ of the model ${C}_{3}$ cars break down during the first year, what is the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year?
question.worked_solution:
Let $B$ be the event that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year, and 

- let ${C}_{1}$ be the event that the car is of model ${C}_{1},$

- let ${C}_{2}$ be the event that the car is of model ${C}_{2},$

- let ${C}_{3}$ be the event that the car is of model ${C}_{3}.$

Then the disjoint union ${C}_{1}⊔{C}_{2}⊔{C}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year, we can use the law of total probability: 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(B) & =P(B\cap {C}_{1})+P(B\cap {C}_{2})+P(B\cap {C}_{3}) \\  & =P(B|{C}_{1})P({C}_{1})+P(B|{C}_{2})P({C}_{2})+P(B|{C}_{3})P({C}_{3})\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since $40%$ of the cars produced by the company are model ${C}_{1},$ and $50%$ are model ${C}_{2},$  the model ${C}_{3}$ cars make up the remaining

$$
100%-(40%+35%)=25%.
$$

As a result, we have

$$
P({C}_{1})=0.4,\,P({C}_{2})=0.35,\,P({C}_{3})=0.25.
$$

- Since $6%$ of the cars of model ${C}_{1},$ $4%$ of those of model  ${C}_{2},$ and $2%$ of the cars of model ${C}_{3}$ break down during the first year, we have

$$
P(B|{C}_{1})=0.06,\,P(B|{C}_{2})=0.04,\,P(B|{C}_{3})=0.02.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year is 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(B) & =P(B|{C}_{1})P({C}_{1})+P(B|{C}_{2})P({C}_{2})+P(B|{C}_{3})P({C}_{3}) \\  & =(0.06)(0.4)+(0.04)(0.35)+(0.02)(0.25) \\  & =0.024+0.014+0.005 \\  & =0.043.\end{aligned}

question.html:
Question 7
?

A company manufactures three types of cars. Of the car population, 40% are model C1, 35% are model C2, and the remaining cars are model C3. If 6% of the model C1, 4% of the model C2, and 2% of the model C3 cars break down during the first year, what is the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year?

a
0.043
b
0.342
c
0.051
d
0.041
e
0.65
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let B be the event that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year, and

  • let C1 be the event that the car is of model C1,

  • let C2 be the event that the car is of model C2,

  • let C3 be the event that the car is of model C3.

Then the disjoint union C1⊔C2⊔C3 covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year, we can use the law of total probability:

P(B)=P(B∩C1)+P(B∩C2)+P(B∩C3)=P(B|C1)P(C1)+P(B|C2)P(C2)+P(B|C3)P(C3)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since 40% of the cars produced by the company are model C1, and 50% are model C2, the model C3 cars make up the remaining 100%−(40%+35%)=25%. As a result, we have P(C1)=0.4,P(C2)=0.35,P(C3)=0.25.

  • Since 6% of the cars of model C1, 4% of those of model C2, and 2% of the cars of model C3 break down during the first year, we have P(B|C1)=0.06,P(B|C2)=0.04,P(B|C3)=0.02.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year is

P(B)=P(B|C1)P(C1)+P(B|C2)P(C2)+P(B|C3)P(C3)=(0.06)(0.4)+(0.04)(0.35)+(0.02)(0.25)=0.024+0.014+0.005=0.043.

Question 7
?

A company manufactures three types of cars. Of the car population, 40% are model C1, 35% are model C2, and the remaining cars are model C3. If 6% of the model C1, 4% of the model C2, and 2% of the model C3 cars break down during the first year, what is the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year?

a
0.043
b
0.342
c
0.051
d
0.041
e
0.65
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let B be the event that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year, and

  • let C1 be the event that the car is of model C1,

  • let C2 be the event that the car is of model C2,

  • let C3 be the event that the car is of model C3.

Then the disjoint union C1⊔C2⊔C3 covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year, we can use the law of total probability:

P(B)=P(B∩C1)+P(B∩C2)+P(B∩C3)=P(B|C1)P(C1)+P(B|C2)P(C2)+P(B|C3)P(C3)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since 40% of the cars produced by the company are model C1, and 50% are model C2, the model C3 cars make up the remaining 100%−(40%+35%)=25%. As a result, we have P(C1)=0.4,P(C2)=0.35,P(C3)=0.25.

  • Since 6% of the cars of model C1, 4% of those of model C2, and 2% of the cars of model C3 break down during the first year, we have P(B|C1)=0.06,P(B|C2)=0.04,P(B|C3)=0.02.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year is

P(B)=P(B|C1)P(C1)+P(B|C2)P(C2)+P(B|C3)P(C3)=(0.06)(0.4)+(0.04)(0.35)+(0.02)(0.25)=0.024+0.014+0.005=0.043.

question.name: Question 8
question.problem: In a particular park, there are three forests. Forest $A$ occupies $40%$ of the park area, and  $30%$ of its plants are poisonous. Forest $B$ occupies $25%$ of the park area, and $20%$ of its plants are poisonous. Forest $C$ occupies the remaining park area, and $6%$ of its plants are poisonous. What is the probability that a randomly selected plant from this park is poisonous? Assume that the plants are evenly distributed throughout the park.
question.worked_solution:
Let $V$ be the event that the plant is poisonous, and 

- let $A$ be the event that the plant is from forest $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the plant is from forest $B,$

- let $C$ be the event that the plant is from forest $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected plant is poisonous, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(V) & =P(V\cap A)+P(V\cap B)+P(V\cap C) \\  & =P(V|A)P(A)+P(V|B)P(B)+P(V|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since forest $A$ occupies $40%$ of the park area and forest $B$ occupies $25%$, then forest $C$ occupies the remaining

$$
100%-(40%+25%)=35%.
$$

As a result, we have

$$
P(A)=0.4,\,P(B)=0.25,\,P(C)=0.35.
$$

- Since $30%$ of the plants in forest $A,$ $20%$ of the plants in forest $B$, and $6%$ of the plants in forrest $C$ are poisonous, we have

$$
P(V|A)=0.3,\,P(V|B)=0.2,\,P(V|C)=0.06.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected plant in that park is poisonous is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(V) & =P(V|A)P(A)+P(V|B)P(B)+P(V|C)P(C) \\  & =(0.3)(0.4)+(0.2)(0.25)+(0.06)(0.35) \\  & =0.12+0.05+0.021 \\  & =0.191.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Three companies supply widgets to a car shop. Company A supplies 45% of the widgets, of which 2% are defective. Company B provides 40% of the widgets, of which 3% are defective. And company C supplies the remaining widgets, of which 4% are defective. What is the probability that a randomly chosen widget from these companies will turn out to be defective?

a
0.421
b
0.085
c
0.027
d
0.152
e
0.211
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let D be the event that the widget is defective, and

  • let A be that the event that the widget was produced by company A,

  • let B be that the event that the widget was produced by company B,

  • let C be that the event that the widget was produced by company C.

Then the disjoint union A⊔B⊔C covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected widget is defective, we can use the law of total probability:

P(D)=P(D∩A)+P(D∩B)+P(D∩C)=P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since Company A supplies 45% and Company B produces 40% of the widgets, then Company B produces the remaining 100%−(45%+40%)=15%. As a result, we have P(A)=0.45,P(B)=0.4,P(C)=0.15.

  • Since 2% of the widgets produced by Company A, 3% of the widgets produced by Company B, and 4% of the widgets produced by Company C, are defective, we have P(D|A)=0.02,P(D|B)=0.03,P(D|C)=0.04.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected widget turns out to be defective is

P(D)=P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C)=(0.02)(0.45)+(0.03)(0.4)+(0.04)(0.15)=0.009+0.012+0.006=0.027.

question.name: Question 10
question.problem: Three bags contain marbles. Bag $1$ contains $12$ red marbles and $8$ green marbles. Bag $2$ contains $14$ red marbles and $6$ green marbles. And bag $3$ contains $10$ red marbles and $10$ green marbles. A bag is selected at random, and a marble is randomly selected from the bag. What is the probability that the marble is red?
question.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be the event of selecting a red marble at random from one of the three bags, and

- let $A$ be the event that the marble is from bag $1,$

- let $B$ be the event that the marble is from bag $2,$

- let $C$ be the event that the marble is from bag $3.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability of selecting a red marble at random from one of the three bags, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(R) & =P(R\cap A)+P(R\cap B)+P(R\cap C) \\  & =P(R|A)P(A)+P(R|B)P(B)+P(R|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since a bag is selected at random, we have

$$
P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

- Since there are $12$ red marbles out of $20$ in bag $1,$ $14$ red marbles out of $20$ in bag $2,$ and $10$ red marbles out of $20$  in bag $3,$ we have 

$$
P(R|A)=\frac{12}{20},\,P(R|B)=\frac{14}{20},\,P(R|C)=\frac{10}{20}.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability of selecting a red marble at random from one of the three bags is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(R) & =P(R|A)P(A)+P(R|B)P(B)+P(R|C)P(C) \\  & =(\frac{12}{20})(\frac{1}{3})+(\frac{14}{20})(\frac{1}{3})+(\frac{10}{20})(\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{12}{60}+\frac{14}{60}+\frac{10}{60} \\  & =\frac{36}{60} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Applying the Law of Total Probability in Terms of Conditional Probability
last_observation.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be the event of selecting a red marble at random from one of the three bags, and

- let $A$ be the event that the marble is from bag $1,$

- let $B$ be the event that the marble is from bag $2,$

- let $C$ be the event that the marble is from bag $3.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability of selecting a red marble at random from one of the three bags, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(R) & =P(R\cap A)+P(R\cap B)+P(R\cap C) \\  & =P(R|A)P(A)+P(R|B)P(B)+P(R|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since a bag is selected at random, we have

$$
P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

- Since there are $12$ red marbles out of $20$ in bag $1,$ $14$ red marbles out of $20$ in bag $2,$ and $10$ red marbles out of $20$  in bag $3,$ we have 

$$
P(R|A)=\frac{12}{20},\,P(R|B)=\frac{14}{20},\,P(R|C)=\frac{10}{20}.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability of selecting a red marble at random from one of the three bags is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(R) & =P(R|A)P(A)+P(R|B)P(B)+P(R|C)P(C) \\  & =(\frac{12}{20})(\frac{1}{3})+(\frac{14}{20})(\frac{1}{3})+(\frac{10}{20})(\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{12}{60}+\frac{14}{60}+\frac{10}{60} \\  & =\frac{36}{60} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 10
?

Three bags contain marbles. Bag 1 contains 12 red marbles and 8 green marbles. Bag 2 contains 14 red marbles and 6 green marbles. And bag 3 contains 10 red marbles and 10 green marbles. A bag is selected at random, and a marble is randomly selected from the bag. What is the probability that the marble is red?

a
34
b
12
c
35
d
16
e
13
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let R be the event of selecting a red marble at random from one of the three bags, and

  • let A be the event that the marble is from bag 1,

  • let B be the event that the marble is from bag 2,

  • let C be the event that the marble is from bag 3.

Then the disjoint union A⊔B⊔C covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability of selecting a red marble at random from one of the three bags, we can use the law of total probability:

P(R)=P(R∩A)+P(R∩B)+P(R∩C)=P(R|A)P(A)+P(R|B)P(B)+P(R|C)P(C)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since a bag is selected at random, we have P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=13.

  • Since there are 12 red marbles out of 20 in bag 1, 14 red marbles out of 20 in bag 2, and 10 red marbles out of 20 in bag 3, we have P(R|A)=1220,P(R|B)=1420,P(R|C)=1020.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability of selecting a red marble at random from one of the three bags is

P(R)=P(R|A)P(A)+P(R|B)P(B)+P(R|C)P(C)=(1220)(13)+(1420)(13)+(1020)(13)=1260+1460+1060=3660=35.

solution.reasoning: Each bag is selected with probability 1/3 and contains 20 marbles. Thus P(red)=(1/3)(12/20+14/20+10/20)=36/60=3/5, option c. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different problem.

Three bags contain marbles. Bag 1 contains 12 red marbles and 8 green marbles. Bag 2 contains 14 red marbles and 6 green marbles. And bag 3 contains 10 red marbles and 10 green marbles. A bag is selected at random, and a marble is randomly selected from the bag. What is the probability that the marble is red?

34
b
12
c
35
d
16
e
13

question.html:
Question 12
?

A company manufactures three types of cars. Of the total car population, 40% are model M1, 35% are model M2, and 25% are model M3. If 6% of model M1 and 4% of model M2 cars break down during the first year, and the probability that a randomly selected car from any of the three models breaks down during the first year is 0.045, what percentage of model M3 cars will break down during the first year?

a
1.4%
b
3.6%
c
2.8%
d
2.6%
e
3.2%
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let B be the event that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year, and

  • let M1 be the event that the car is model M1,

  • let M2 be the event that the car is model M2,

  • let M3 be the event that the car is model M3.

Then the disjoint union M1⊔M2⊔M3 covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected car will break down during the first year, we can use the law of total probability:

P(B)=P(B∩M1)+P(B∩M2)+P(B∩M3)=P(B|M1)P(M1)+P(B|M2)P(M2)+P(B|M3)P(M3)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since 40% of cars are model M1,, 35% are model M2, and 25% are model M3, we have P(M1)=0.4,P(M2)=0.35,P(M3)=0.25.

  • Since 6% of model M1 and 4% of model M2 break down during the first year, we have P(B|M1)=0.06,P(B|M2)=0.04.

  • Since the probability that a randomly selected car breaks down during the first year is 0.045, we have P(B)=0.045.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for P(B|M3), we get

P(B)=P(B|M1)P(M1)+P(B|M2)P(M2)+P(B|M3)P(M3)0.045=(0.06)(0.4)+(0.04)(0.35)+P(B|M3)(0.25)0.045=0.024+0.014+0.25P(B|M3)0.25P(B|M3)=0.007P(B|M3)=0.028=2.8%

Therefore, 2.8% of model M3 cars break down during the first year.

question.name: Question 13
question.problem: Three similar bags, $A,\,B$, and $C,$ contain balls. Bag $A$ contains $4$ red and $6$ green balls, and bag $B$ contains $6$ red and $4$ green balls. A bag is selected at random, and a ball is randomly selected from the bag. If the probability that the selected ball is green is $\frac{3}{5},$ what proportion of balls from bag $C$ are green?
question.worked_solution:
Let $G$ be the event of selecting a green ball at random from one of the three bags, and

- let $A$ be the event that the ball is from bag $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the ball is from $B,$

- let $C$ be the event that the ball is from bag $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability of selecting a green ball, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G) & =P(G\cap A)+P(G\cap B)+P(G\cap C) \\  & =P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since a bag is selected at random, we have

$$
P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

- Since there are $6$ green balls out of $10$ in bag $A,$ and $4$ green balls out of $10$ in bag $B,$ we have

$$
P(G|A)=\frac{6}{10},\,P(G|B)=\frac{4}{10}.
$$

- Since the probability of choosing a green ball is $\frac{3}{5},$ we have

$$
P(G)=\frac{3}{5}.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(G|C),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G) & =P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C) \\ \frac{3}{5} & =(\frac{6}{10})(\frac{1}{3})+(\frac{4}{10})(\frac{1}{3})+P(G|C)(\frac{1}{3}) \\ \frac{3}{5} & =\frac{1}{5}+\frac{2}{15}+(\frac{1}{3})P(G|C) \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot P(G|C) & =\frac{3}{5}-\frac{1}{5}-\frac{2}{15} \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot P(G|C) & =\frac{4}{15} \\ P(G|C) & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\frac{4}{5}$ of the balls in bag $C$ are green.

Question 13

Three similar bags, A,B, and C, contain balls. Bag A contains 4 red and 6 green balls, and bag B contains 6 red and 4 green balls. A bag is selected at random, and a ball is randomly selected from the bag. If the probability that the selected ball is green is 35, what proportion of balls from bag C are green?

a
45
b
25
c
15
d
35
e
910
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let G be the event of selecting a green ball at random from one of the three bags, and

  • let A be the event that the ball is from bag A,

  • let B be the event that the ball is from B,

  • let C be the event that the ball is from bag C.

Then the disjoint union A⊔B⊔C covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability of selecting a green ball, we can use the law of total probability:

P(G)=P(G∩A)+P(G∩B)+P(G∩C)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since a bag is selected at random, we have P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=13.

  • Since there are 6 green balls out of 10 in bag A, and 4 green balls out of 10 in bag B, we have P(G|A)=610,P(G|B)=410.

  • Since the probability of choosing a green ball is 35, we have P(G)=35.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for P(G|C), we get

P(G)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)35=(610)(13)+(410)(13)+P(G|C)(13)35=15+215+(13)P(G|C)13⋅P(G|C)=35−15−21513⋅P(G|C)=415P(G|C)=45.

last_observation.worked_solution:
Let $G$ be the event of selecting a green ball at random from one of the three bags, and

- let $A$ be the event that the ball is from bag $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the ball is from $B,$

- let $C$ be the event that the ball is from bag $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability of selecting a green ball, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G) & =P(G\cap A)+P(G\cap B)+P(G\cap C) \\  & =P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since a bag is selected at random, we have

$$
P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

- Since there are $6$ green balls out of $10$ in bag $A,$ and $4$ green balls out of $10$ in bag $B,$ we have

$$
P(G|A)=\frac{6}{10},\,P(G|B)=\frac{4}{10}.
$$

- Since the probability of choosing a green ball is $\frac{3}{5},$ we have

$$
P(G)=\frac{3}{5}.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(G|C),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G) & =P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C) \\ \frac{3}{5} & =(\frac{6}{10})(\frac{1}{3})+(\frac{4}{10})(\frac{1}{3})+P(G|C)(\frac{1}{3}) \\ \frac{3}{5} & =\frac{1}{5}+\frac{2}{15}+(\frac{1}{3})P(G|C) \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot P(G|C) & =\frac{3}{5}-\frac{1}{5}-\frac{2}{15} \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot P(G|C) & =\frac{4}{15} \\ P(G|C) & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\frac{4}{5}$ of the balls in bag $C$ are green.

Question 13
?

Three similar bags, A,B, and C, contain balls. Bag A contains 4 red and 6 green balls, and bag B contains 6 red and 4 green balls. A bag is selected at random, and a ball is randomly selected from the bag. If the probability that the selected ball is green is 35, what proportion of balls from bag C are green?

a
45
b
25
c
15
d
35
e
910
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let G be the event of selecting a green ball at random from one of the three bags, and

  • let A be the event that the ball is from bag A,

  • let B be the event that the ball is from B,

  • let C be the event that the ball is from bag C.

Then the disjoint union A⊔B⊔C covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability of selecting a green ball, we can use the law of total probability:

P(G)=P(G∩A)+P(G∩B)+P(G∩C)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since a bag is selected at random, we have P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=13.

  • Since there are 6 green balls out of 10 in bag A, and 4 green balls out of 10 in bag B, we have P(G|A)=610,P(G|B)=410.

  • Since the probability of choosing a green ball is 35, we have P(G)=35.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for P(G|C), we get

P(G)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)35=(610)(13)+(410)(13)+P(G|C)(13)35=15+215+(13)P(G|C)13⋅P(G|C)=35−15−21513⋅P(G|C)=415P(G|C)=45.

Therefore, 45 of the balls in bag C are green.

Question 13
?

Three similar bags, A,B, and C, contain balls. Bag A contains 4 red and 6 green balls, and bag B contains 6 red and 4 green balls. A bag is selected at random, and a ball is randomly selected from the bag. If the probability that the selected ball is green is 35, what proportion of balls from bag C are green?

a
45
b
25
c
15
d
35
e
910
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let G be the event of selecting a green ball at random from one of the three bags, and

  • let A be the event that the ball is from bag A,

  • let B be the event that the ball is from B,

  • let C be the event that the ball is from bag C.

Then the disjoint union A⊔B⊔C covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability of selecting a green ball, we can use the law of total probability:

P(G)=P(G∩A)+P(G∩B)+P(G∩C)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since a bag is selected at random, we have P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=13.

  • Since there are 6 green balls out of 10 in bag A, and 4 green balls out of 10 in bag B, we have P(G|A)=610,P(G|B)=410.

  • Since the probability of choosing a green ball is 35, we have P(G)=35.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for P(G|C), we get

P(G)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)35=(610)(13)+(410)(13)+P(G|C)(13)35=15+215+(13)P(G|C)13⋅P(G|C)=35−15−21513⋅P(G|C)=415P(G|C)=45.

Therefore, 45 of the balls in bag C are green.

question.name: Question 14
question.problem: In a particular national park, there are three forests. Forest $A$ occupies $40%$ of the park's total area, and $30%$ of the plants it contains are poisonous, while forest $B$ occupies $25%$ of the park's total area, and $20%$ of the plants it has are poisonous. Forest $C$ occupies the remaining area of the park. If the probability that a randomly selected plant from the park is poisonous is $0.24,$ what percentage of plants from forest $C$ are poisonous? Assume that the plants are evenly distributed throughout the park.
question.worked_solution:
Let $V$ be the event that a randomly selected plant is poisonous, and 

- let $A$ be the event that the plant is from forest $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the plant is from forest $B,$

- let $C$ be the event that the plant is from forest $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space. 

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected plant is poisonous, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(V) & =P(V\cap A)+P(V\cap B)+P(V\cap C) \\  & =P(V|A)P(A)+P(V|B)P(B)+P(V|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.  

- Since forest $A$ occupies $40%$ of the total park land and  forest $B$ occupies $25%$, then forest $C$ occupies the remaining

$$
100%-(40%+25%)=35%.
$$

As a result, we have

$$
P(A)=0.4,\,P(B)=0.25,\,P(C)=0.35.
$$

- Since $30%$ of the plants in forest $A$ and $20%$ of the plants in forest $B$ are poisonous, we have

$$
P(V|A)=0.3,\,P(V|B)=0.2
$$

- Since the probability that a randomly selected plant from the park is poisonous is $0.24,$ we have

$$
P(V)=0.24.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(V|C),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(V) & =P(V|A)P(A)+P(V|B)P(B)+P(V|C)P(C) \\ 0.24 & =(0.3)(0.4)+(0.2)(0.25)+P(V|C)(0.35) \\ 0.24 & =0.12+0.05+0.35P(V|C) \\ 0.35P(V|C) & =0.07 \\ P(V|C) & =0.2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $20%$ of plants from forest $C$ are poisonous.

Forest C occupies the remaining area of the park. If the probability that a randomly selected plant from the park is poisonous is 0.24, what percentage of plants from forest C are poisonous? Assume that the plants are evenly distributed throughout the park.

a
20%
b
25%
c
18%
d
12%
e
22%
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let V be the event that a randomly selected plant is poisonous, and

  • let A be the event that the plant is from forest A,

  • let B be the event that the plant is from forest B,

  • let C be the event that the plant is from forest C.

Then the disjoint union A⊔B⊔C covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected plant is poisonous, we can use the law of total probability:

P(V)=P(V∩A)+P(V∩B)+P(V∩C)=P(V|A)P(A)+P(V|B)P(B)+P(V|C)P(C)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since forest A occupies 40% of the total park land and forest B occupies 25%, then forest C occupies the remaining 100%−(40%+25%)=35%. As a result, we have P(A)=0.4,P(B)=0.25,P(C)=0.35.

  • Since 30% of the plants in forest A and 20% of the plants in forest B are poisonous, we have P(V|A)=0.3,P(V|B)=0.2

  • Since the probability that a randomly selected plant from the park is poisonous is 0.24, we have P(V)=0.24.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for P(V|C), we get

P(V)=P(V|A)P(A)+P(V|B)P(B)+P(V|C)P(C)0.24=(0.3)(0.4)+(0.2)(0.25)+P(V|C)(0.35)0.24=0.12+0.05+0.35P(V|C)0.35P(V|C)=0.07P(V|C)=0.2

Therefore, 20% of plants from forest C are poisonous.

question.name: Question 15
question.problem: Three bags, $A,B,$ and $C,$ contain marbles. Bag $A$ contains $12$ red and $8$ green marbles, while bag $B$ contains $14$ red and $6$ green marbles. A bag is selected at random, and a marble is randomly selected from the bag. If the probability that the selected marble is green is $\frac{2}{5},$  what proportion of marbles from bag $C$ are green?
question.worked_solution:
Let $G$ be the event of selecting a green marble at random from one of the three bags, and 

- let $A$ be the event that the marble is from bag $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the marble is from bag $B,$

- let $C$ be the event that the marble is from bag $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space. 

To calculate the probability of selecting a green marble, we can use the law of total probability: 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G) & =P(G\cap A)+P(G\cap B)+P(G\cap C) \\  & =P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since a bag is selected at random, we have

$$
P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

- Since there are $8$ green marbles out of $20$  in bag $A,$ and  $6$ green marbles out of $20$  in bag $B,$ we have 

$$
P(G|A)=\frac{8}{20},\,P(G|B)=\frac{6}{20}.
$$

- Since the probability of picking a green marble  from one of the bags is $\frac{2}{5},$ we have

$$
P(G)=\frac{2}{5}.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(G|C),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G) & =P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C) \\ \frac{2}{5} & =(\frac{8}{20})(\frac{1}{3})+(\frac{6}{20})(\frac{1}{3})+P(G|C)(\frac{1}{3}) \\ \frac{2}{5} & =\frac{2}{15}+\frac{1}{10}+(\frac{1}{3})P(G|C) \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot P(G|C) & =\frac{2}{5}-\frac{2}{15}-\frac{1}{10} \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot P(G|C) & =\frac{1}{6} \\ P(G|C) & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\frac{1}{2}$ of the marbles from bag $C$ are green.

last_observation.worked_solution:
Let $G$ be the event of selecting a green marble at random from one of the three bags, and 

- let $A$ be the event that the marble is from bag $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the marble is from bag $B,$

- let $C$ be the event that the marble is from bag $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space. 

To calculate the probability of selecting a green marble, we can use the law of total probability: 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G) & =P(G\cap A)+P(G\cap B)+P(G\cap C) \\  & =P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since a bag is selected at random, we have

$$
P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=\frac{1}{3}.
$$

- Since there are $8$ green marbles out of $20$  in bag $A,$ and  $6$ green marbles out of $20$  in bag $B,$ we have 

$$
P(G|A)=\frac{8}{20},\,P(G|B)=\frac{6}{20}.
$$

- Since the probability of picking a green marble  from one of the bags is $\frac{2}{5},$ we have

$$
P(G)=\frac{2}{5}.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(G|C),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(G) & =P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C) \\ \frac{2}{5} & =(\frac{8}{20})(\frac{1}{3})+(\frac{6}{20})(\frac{1}{3})+P(G|C)(\frac{1}{3}) \\ \frac{2}{5} & =\frac{2}{15}+\frac{1}{10}+(\frac{1}{3})P(G|C) \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot P(G|C) & =\frac{2}{5}-\frac{2}{15}-\frac{1}{10} \\ \frac{1}{3}\cdot P(G|C) & =\frac{1}{6} \\ P(G|C) & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\frac{1}{2}$ of the marbles from bag $C$ are green.

question.html:
Question 15
?

Three bags, A,B, and C, contain marbles. Bag A contains 12 red and 8 green marbles, while bag B contains 14 red and 6 green marbles. A bag is selected at random, and a marble is randomly selected from the bag. If the probability that the selected marble is green is 25, what proportion of marbles from bag C are green?

a
45
b
12
c
35
d
13
e
710
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let G be the event of selecting a green marble at random from one of the three bags, and

  • let A be the event that the marble is from bag A,

  • let B be the event that the marble is from bag B,

  • let C be the event that the marble is from bag C.

Then the disjoint union A⊔B⊔C covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability of selecting a green marble, we can use the law of total probability:

P(G)=P(G∩A)+P(G∩B)+P(G∩C)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

  • Since a bag is selected at random, we have P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=13.

  • Since there are 8 green marbles out of 20 in bag A, and 6 green marbles out of 20 in bag B, we have P(G|A)=820,P(G|B)=620.

  • Since the probability of picking a green marble from one of the bags is 25, we have P(G)=25.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for P(G|C), we get

P(G)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)25=(820)(13)+(620)(13)+P(G|C)(13)25=215+110+(13)P(G|C)13⋅P(G|C)=25−215−11013⋅P(G|C)=16P(G|C)=12.

Therefore, 12 of the marbles from bag C are green.

solution.reasoning: Each bag is selected with probability 1/3. Let x be the green proportion in bag C. Then 2/5=(1/3)(8/20+6/20+x), so x=6/5−2/5−3/10=1/2, option b. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured; the worked example concerns a different problem.

  • Since the probability of picking a green marble from one of the bags is 25, we have P(G)=25.

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for P(G|C), we get

P(G)=P(G|A)P(A)+P(G|B)P(B)+P(G|C)P(C)25=(820)(13)+(620)(13)+P(G|C)(13)25=215+110+(13)P(G|C)13⋅P(G|C)=25−215−11013⋅P(G|C)=16P(G|C)=12.

Therefore, 12 of the marbles from bag C are green.

questions.name: Question 2
questions.problem:
The recursive formula for the Fibonacci numbers is 

$$
{a}_{n+2}={a}_{n+1}+{a}_{n},\,{a}_{1}={a}_{2}=1,\,n\ge 1.
$$

What is the eighth number in the sequence?
questions.worked_solution:
Substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1+2} & ={a}_{1+1}+{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{3} & ={a}_{2}+{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{3} & =1+1 \\ {a}_{3} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=2$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2+2} & ={a}_{2+1}+{a}_{2} \\ {a}_{4} & ={a}_{3}+{a}_{2} \\ {a}_{4} & =2+1 \\ {a}_{4} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=3$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3+2} & ={a}_{3+1}+{a}_{3} \\ {a}_{5} & ={a}_{4}+{a}_{3} \\ {a}_{5} & =3+2 \\ {a}_{5} & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=4$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{4+2} & ={a}_{4+1}+{a}_{4} \\ {a}_{6} & ={a}_{5}+{a}_{4} \\ {a}_{6} & =5+3 \\ {a}_{6} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=5$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{5+2} & ={a}_{5+1}+{a}_{5} \\ {a}_{7} & ={a}_{6}+{a}_{5} \\ {a}_{7} & =8+5 \\ {a}_{7} & =13\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=6$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{6+2} & ={a}_{6+1}+{a}_{6} \\ {a}_{8} & ={a}_{7}+{a}_{6} \\ {a}_{8} & =13+8 \\ {a}_{8} & =21\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $21$ is the eighth number in the sequence.

questions.name: Question 3
questions.worked_solution:
The recursion relation is

$$
f(n+2)=f(n+1)+f(n).
$$

Substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1+2) & =f(1+1)+f(1) \\ f(3) & =f(2)+f(1) \\ f(3) & =(-2)+7 \\ f(3) & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=2$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2+2) & =f(2+1)+f(2) \\ f(4) & =f(3)+f(2) \\ f(4) & =5+(-2) \\ f(4) & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, substituting $n=3,4,5,6$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(5) & =f(3+2)=f(3+1)+f(3)=f(4)+f(3)=3+5=8, \\ f(6) & =f(4+2)=f(4+1)+f(4)=f(5)+f(4)=8+3=11, \\ f(7) & =f(5+2)=f(5+1)+f(5)=f(6)+f(5)=11+8=19, \\ f(8) & =f(6+2)=f(6+1)+f(6)=f(7)+f(6)=19+11=30.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(8)=30.$

EXPLANATION

To compute a4, we first need to compute a3. So, we substitute n=1 into the recursive formula, as follows:

Next, to compute a4, we substitute n=2 into the recursive formula: a2+2=a2+1+a2a4=a3+a2a4=0+1a4=1

The recursive formula for the Fibonacci numbers is an+2=an+1+an,a1=a2=1,n≥1.

What is the eighth number in the sequence?

a
34
b
8
c
21
d
13
e
55
Submit

EXPLANATION

Substituting n=1 into the recursive formula gives: a1+2=a1+1+a1a3=a2+a1a3=1+1a3=2

Substituting n=2 into the recursive formula gives: a2+2=a2+1+a2a4=a3+a2a4=2+1a4=3

Substituting n=3 into the recursive formula gives: a3+2=a3+1+a3a5=a4+a3a5=3+2a5=5

Substituting n=4 into the recursive formula gives:

a4+2=a4+1+a4a6=a5+a4a6=5+3a6=8

Substituting n=5 into the recursive formula gives: a5+2=a5+1+a5a7=a6+a5a7=8+5a7=13

Substituting n=6 into the recursive formula gives:

a6+2=a6+1+a6a8=a7+a6a8=13+8a8=21

Therefore, 21 is the eighth number in the sequence.

observed_steps.name: Question 3
observed_steps.worked_solution:
The recursion relation is

$$
f(n+2)=f(n+1)+f(n).
$$

Substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1+2) & =f(1+1)+f(1) \\ f(3) & =f(2)+f(1) \\ f(3) & =(-2)+7 \\ f(3) & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=2$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2+2) & =f(2+1)+f(2) \\ f(4) & =f(3)+f(2) \\ f(4) & =5+(-2) \\ f(4) & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, substituting $n=3,4,5,6$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(5) & =f(3+2)=f(3+1)+f(3)=f(4)+f(3)=3+5=8, \\ f(6) & =f(4+2)=f(4+1)+f(4)=f(5)+f(4)=8+3=11, \\ f(7) & =f(5+2)=f(5+1)+f(5)=f(6)+f(5)=11+8=19, \\ f(8) & =f(6+2)=f(6+1)+f(6)=f(7)+f(6)=19+11=30.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(8)=30.$

question.worked_solution:
The recursion relation is

$$
f(n+2)=f(n+1)+f(n).
$$

Substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1+2) & =f(1+1)+f(1) \\ f(3) & =f(2)+f(1) \\ f(3) & =(-2)+7 \\ f(3) & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=2$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2+2) & =f(2+1)+f(2) \\ f(4) & =f(3)+f(2) \\ f(4) & =5+(-2) \\ f(4) & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, substituting $n=3,4,5,6$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(5) & =f(3+2)=f(3+1)+f(3)=f(4)+f(3)=3+5=8, \\ f(6) & =f(4+2)=f(4+1)+f(4)=f(5)+f(4)=8+3=11, \\ f(7) & =f(5+2)=f(5+1)+f(5)=f(6)+f(5)=11+8=19, \\ f(8) & =f(6+2)=f(6+1)+f(6)=f(7)+f(6)=19+11=30.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(8)=30.$

questions.name: Question 1
questions.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t)+\overset{f(t)}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}},\,Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations and the fundamental matrix of the corresponding homogeneous system above. Using the method of variation of parameters, compute ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)$ and the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t)$ of the system.
${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)=\,\,$ $5{e}^{-t}$ $\,,\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=\,\,$ $-4$
{{field-1}} {{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{3t}-({e}^{3t})\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-t} \\ -3{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-t} \\ -3{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 5{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -3{e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5{e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5{e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 2
questions.problem:
Consider the following system of differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t),$ where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and $u(t)$ is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for ${x}_{p}(t)$ is given below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t)$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{p}^{′}(t)=Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)$

$\text{L6}:\,$ ${u}^{′}(t)={Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that {{field-1}} matrix.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from lines {{field-2}} by substitution.

$\,$ Line $\text{L7}$ follows from line $\text{L6}$ by {{field-3}} both sides of the equation.

$\,$ Line $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting {{field-4}} into $\text{L1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's examine each statement in turn.

- We first consider line $\text{L4}.$ Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ i.e., by substituting any column $c(t)$ of $Φ$ into the homogeneous system, we get

$$
{c}^{′}(t)=Ac(t),
$$

where ${c}^{′}(t)$ is the corresponding column of derivatives in $Φ.$ As a result, this means that ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ.$ Therefore, $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that $Φ\text{ is a fundamental}$ matrix.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L3}$, $\text{L4},$ and $\text{L5}.$ Let's substitute ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$ from $\text{L4}$ into $\text{L3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)+\cancel{AΦu(t)}=\cancel{AΦu(t)}+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L5}$ follows from $\text{L3}\text{ and }\text{L4}$ by substitution.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L6}$ and $\text{L7}.$ To get $\text{L7},$ we are $\text{integrating}$ both sides of the equation in $\text{L6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {u}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t & =\int {Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)\,\text{d}t \\ u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L1},$ $\text{L7},$ and $\text{L8}.$ Substituting

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

from $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φu(t) \\  & =Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1}.$

2.Constructing the Formulas for Variation of Parameters?

Consider the following system of differential equations: x′(t)=Ax(t)+f(t) Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form xp(t)=Φu(t), where Φ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and u(t) is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for xp(t) is given below.

L1: xp(t)=Φu(t)

L2: xp′(t)=Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)

L3: Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)

L4: Φ′=AΦ

L5: Φu′(t)=f(t)

L6: u′(t)=Φ−1(t)f(t)

L7: u(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt

questions.name: Question 3
questions.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -5 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+\overset{f(t)}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 4{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]}},\,Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{-t} & -3{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations and the fundamental matrix of the corresponding homogeneous system above. Using the method of variation of parameters, compute ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)$ and the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t)$ of the system.
${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,,\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)={e}^{t}\,\,$ {{field-2}}
$\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}$ $\frac{17}{6}$
questions.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{-t} & -3{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 4{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{0\cdot (-3{e}^{4t})-3{e}^{4t}\cdot {e}^{-t}}[\begin{aligned}-3{e}^{4t} & -3{e}^{4t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-3t}}{3}[\begin{aligned}-3{e}^{4t} & -3{e}^{4t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-4t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-4t} & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 4{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 5{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{-t} & -3{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{t} \\ \frac{17}{6}{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{17}{6}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 4
questions.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form
$x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+\,\,\frac{1}{3}$ {{field-1}} .
$3(t-1)$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3t} & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-3t}\cdot {e}^{-t}-0}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]. \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3t{e}^{3t} \\ t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}3t{e}^{3t} \\ t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 3t{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=3t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=3\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3t{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t & =(3t)\cdot \frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}-\int \frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}(3\,\text{d}t) \\  & =t{e}^{3t}-\int {e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =t{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}(3t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=1\,\text{d}t$ and $v={e}^{t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t & =t\cdot {e}^{t}-\int {e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =t{e}^{t}-{e}^{t} \\  & ={e}^{t}(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3t} & 0 \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{3t}(3t-1) \\ {e}^{t}(t-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}3t-1 \\ 3(t-1)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 5
questions.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form
$x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+\,\,\frac{1}{2}$ {{field-1}} .
$6t-6$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}t \\ 3t\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-2t}\cdot {e}^{-t}-{e}^{-t}\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{3t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -{e}^{2t} \\ 0 & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -{e}^{2t} \\ 0 & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2t{e}^{2t} \\ 3t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}-2t{e}^{2t} \\ 3t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int -2t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int 3t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=-2t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=-2\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -2t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t & =(-2t)\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}-\int \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}\cdot (-2\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-t{e}^{2t}+\int {e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-t{e}^{2t}+\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}(1-2t).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=3t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=3\,\text{d}t$ and $v={e}^{t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t & =(3t)\cdot {e}^{t}-\int {e}^{t}\cdot (3\,\text{d}t) \\  & =3t{e}^{t}-3{e}^{t} \\  & =3{e}^{t}(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}(1-2t) \\ 3{e}^{t}(t-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}(1-2t)+6(t-1) \\ 6(t-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4t-5 \\ 6t-6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

observed_steps.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{3t}-({e}^{3t})\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -{e}^{-t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-t} \\ -3{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-t} \\ -3{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 5{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -3{e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5{e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5{e}^{-t} \\ {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form xp(t)=Φu(t) where Φ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, f(t) is the forcing column vector and u(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt.

In our case, Φ=[ete3t0e3t],f(t)=[2−3].

Since Φ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a 2×2 matrix, we get the following: Φ−1=1et⋅e3t−(e3t)⋅0[e3t−e3t0et]=e−4t[e3t−e3t0et]=[e−t−e−t0e−3t]Φ−1f(t)=[e−t−e−t0e−3t][2−3]=[5e−t−3e−3t]

observed_steps.name: Question 2
observed_steps.worked_solution:
Let's examine each statement in turn.

- We first consider line $\text{L4}.$ Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ i.e., by substituting any column $c(t)$ of $Φ$ into the homogeneous system, we get

$$
{c}^{′}(t)=Ac(t),
$$

where ${c}^{′}(t)$ is the corresponding column of derivatives in $Φ.$ As a result, this means that ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ.$ Therefore, $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that $Φ\text{ is a fundamental}$ matrix.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L3}$, $\text{L4},$ and $\text{L5}.$ Let's substitute ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$ from $\text{L4}$ into $\text{L3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)+\cancel{AΦu(t)}=\cancel{AΦu(t)}+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L5}$ follows from $\text{L3}\text{ and }\text{L4}$ by substitution.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L6}$ and $\text{L7}.$ To get $\text{L7},$ we are $\text{integrating}$ both sides of the equation in $\text{L6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {u}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t & =\int {Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)\,\text{d}t \\ u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L1},$ $\text{L7},$ and $\text{L8}.$ Substituting

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

from $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φu(t) \\  & =Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1}.$

question.name: Question 2
question.problem:
Consider the following system of differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t),$ where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and $u(t)$ is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for ${x}_{p}(t)$ is given below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t)$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{p}^{′}(t)=Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)$

$\text{L6}:\,$ ${u}^{′}(t)={Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that {{field-1}} matrix.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from lines {{field-2}} by substitution.

$\,$ Line $\text{L7}$ follows from line $\text{L6}$ by {{field-3}} both sides of the equation.

$\,$ Line $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting {{field-4}} into $\text{L1}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine each statement in turn.

- We first consider line $\text{L4}.$ Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ i.e., by substituting any column $c(t)$ of $Φ$ into the homogeneous system, we get

$$
{c}^{′}(t)=Ac(t),
$$

where ${c}^{′}(t)$ is the corresponding column of derivatives in $Φ.$ As a result, this means that ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ.$ Therefore, $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that $Φ\text{ is a fundamental}$ matrix.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L3}$, $\text{L4},$ and $\text{L5}.$ Let's substitute ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$ from $\text{L4}$ into $\text{L3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)+\cancel{AΦu(t)}=\cancel{AΦu(t)}+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L5}$ follows from $\text{L3}\text{ and }\text{L4}$ by substitution.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L6}$ and $\text{L7}.$ To get $\text{L7},$ we are $\text{integrating}$ both sides of the equation in $\text{L6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {u}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t & =\int {Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)\,\text{d}t \\ u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L1},$ $\text{L7},$ and $\text{L8}.$ Substituting

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

from $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φu(t) \\  & =Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1}.$

Question 2
?
Consider the following system of differential equations: x′(t)=Ax(t)+f(t) Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form xp(t)=Φu(t), where Φ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and u(t) is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for xp(t) is given below.

L1: xp(t)=Φu(t)

L2: xp′(t)=Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)

L3: Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)

L4: Φ′=AΦ

L5: Φu′(t)=f(t)

L6: u′(t)=Φ−1(t)f(t)

L7: u(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt

L8: xp(t)=Φ∫Φ−1f(t)dt

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

Line L4 follows from the fact that
Φ is a fundamental
Φ is a square
A is the identity
A is an invertible
Φ is a fundamental
matrix.

Line L5 follows from lines
L3 and L4
L2 and L3
L2 and L4
L1 and L4
L3 and L4
by substitution.

Line L7 follows from line L6 by
integrating
differentiating
integrating
adding Φ
pre-multiplying by Φ−1
both sides of the equation.

Line L8 is obtained by substituting
L7
L2
L7
L5
L6
into L1.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's examine each statement in turn.

  • We first consider line L4. Since Φ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t), i.e., by substituting any column c(t) of Φ into the homogeneous system, we get c′(t)=Ac(t), where c′(t) is the corresponding column of derivatives in Φ. As a result, this means that Φ′=AΦ. Therefore, L4 follows from the fact that Φ is a fundamental matrix.

  • Next, we consider lines L3, L4, and L5. Let's substitute Φ′=AΦ from L4 into L3: Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)Φu′(t)+AΦu(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)Φu′(t)=f(t) Therefore, L5 follows from L3 and L4 by substitution.

  • Next, we consider lines L6 and L7. To get L7, we are integrating both sides of the equation in L6: ∫u′(t)dt=∫Φ−1(t)f(t)dtu(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt

  • Finally, we consider lines L1, L7, and L8. Substituting u(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt from L7 into L1, we get xp(t)=Φu(t)=Φ∫Φ−1f(t)dt. Therefore, L8 is obtained by substituting L7 into L1.

observed_steps.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{-t} & -3{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 4{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{0\cdot (-3{e}^{4t})-3{e}^{4t}\cdot {e}^{-t}}[\begin{aligned}-3{e}^{4t} & -3{e}^{4t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-3t}}{3}[\begin{aligned}-3{e}^{4t} & -3{e}^{4t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-4t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-4t} & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 4{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 5{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{-t} & -3{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{t} \\ \frac{17}{6}{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{17}{6}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

observed_steps.name: Question 4
observed_steps.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$

question.name: Question 2
question.problem:
Consider the following system of differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t),$ where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and $u(t)$ is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for ${x}_{p}(t)$ is given below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t)$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{p}^{′}(t)=Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)$

$\text{L6}:\,$ ${u}^{′}(t)={Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that {{field-1}} matrix.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from lines {{field-2}} by substitution.

$\,$ Line $\text{L7}$ follows from line $\text{L6}$ by {{field-3}} both sides of the equation.

$\,$ Line $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting {{field-4}} into $\text{L1}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine each statement in turn.

- We first consider line $\text{L4}.$ Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ i.e., by substituting any column $c(t)$ of $Φ$ into the homogeneous system, we get

$$
{c}^{′}(t)=Ac(t),
$$

where ${c}^{′}(t)$ is the corresponding column of derivatives in $Φ.$ As a result, this means that ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ.$ Therefore, $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that $Φ\text{ is a fundamental}$ matrix.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L3}$, $\text{L4},$ and $\text{L5}.$ Let's substitute ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$ from $\text{L4}$ into $\text{L3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)+\cancel{AΦu(t)}=\cancel{AΦu(t)}+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L5}$ follows from $\text{L3}\text{ and }\text{L4}$ by substitution.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L6}$ and $\text{L7}.$ To get $\text{L7},$ we are $\text{integrating}$ both sides of the equation in $\text{L6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {u}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t & =\int {Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)\,\text{d}t \\ u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L1},$ $\text{L7},$ and $\text{L8}.$ Substituting

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

from $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φu(t) \\  & =Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1}.$

Question 2
?
Consider the following system of differential equations: x′(t)=Ax(t)+f(t) Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form xp(t)=Φu(t), where Φ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and u(t) is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for xp(t) is given below.

L1: xp(t)=Φu(t)

L2: xp′(t)=Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)

L3: Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)

L4: Φ′=AΦ

L5: Φu′(t)=f(t)

L6: u′(t)=Φ−1(t)f(t)

L7: u(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt

L8: xp(t)=Φ∫Φ−1f(t)dt

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

Line L4 follows from the fact that
Φ is a fundamental
Φ is a square
A is the identity
A is an invertible
Φ is a fundamental
matrix.

Line L5 follows from lines
L3 and L4
L2 and L3
L2 and L4
L1 and L4
L3 and L4
by substitution.

Line L7 follows from line L6 by
integrating
differentiating
integrating
adding Φ
pre-multiplying by Φ−1
both sides of the equation.

Line L8 is obtained by substituting
L7
L2
L7
L5
L6
into L1.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's examine each statement in turn.

  • We first consider line L4. Since Φ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t), i.e., by substituting any column c(t) of Φ into the homogeneous system, we get c′(t)=Ac(t), where c′(t) is the corresponding column of derivatives in Φ. As a result, this means that Φ′=AΦ. Therefore, L4 follows from the fact that Φ is a fundamental matrix.

  • Next, we consider lines L3, L4, and L5. Let's substitute Φ′=AΦ from L4 into L3: Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)Φu′(t)+AΦu(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)Φu′(t)=f(t) Therefore, L5 follows from L3 and L4 by substitution.

  • Next, we consider lines L6 and L7. To get L7, we are integrating both sides of the equation in L6: ∫u′(t)dt=∫Φ−1(t)f(t)dtu(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt

  • Finally, we consider lines L1, L7, and L8. Substituting u(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt from L7 into L1, we get xp(t)=Φu(t)=Φ∫Φ−1f(t)dt. Therefore, L8 is obtained by substituting L7 into L1.

last_observation.name: Question 2
last_observation.worked_solution:
Let's examine each statement in turn.

- We first consider line $\text{L4}.$ Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ i.e., by substituting any column $c(t)$ of $Φ$ into the homogeneous system, we get

$$
{c}^{′}(t)=Ac(t),
$$

where ${c}^{′}(t)$ is the corresponding column of derivatives in $Φ.$ As a result, this means that ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ.$ Therefore, $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that $Φ\text{ is a fundamental}$ matrix.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L3}$, $\text{L4},$ and $\text{L5}.$ Let's substitute ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$ from $\text{L4}$ into $\text{L3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)+\cancel{AΦu(t)}=\cancel{AΦu(t)}+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L5}$ follows from $\text{L3}\text{ and }\text{L4}$ by substitution.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L6}$ and $\text{L7}.$ To get $\text{L7},$ we are $\text{integrating}$ both sides of the equation in $\text{L6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {u}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t & =\int {Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)\,\text{d}t \\ u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L1},$ $\text{L7},$ and $\text{L8}.$ Substituting

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

from $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φu(t) \\  & =Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1}.$

question.name: Question 2
question.problem:
Consider the following system of differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t),$ where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and $u(t)$ is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for ${x}_{p}(t)$ is given below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t)$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{p}^{′}(t)=Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)$

$\text{L6}:\,$ ${u}^{′}(t)={Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that {{field-1}} matrix.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from lines {{field-2}} by substitution.

$\,$ Line $\text{L7}$ follows from line $\text{L6}$ by {{field-3}} both sides of the equation.

$\,$ Line $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting {{field-4}} into $\text{L1}.$

Consider the following system of differential equations: x′(t)=Ax(t)+f(t) Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form xp(t)=Φu(t), where Φ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and u(t) is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for xp(t) is given below.

L1: xp(t)=Φu(t)

L2: xp′(t)=Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)

L3: Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)

L4: Φ′=AΦ

L5: Φu′(t)=f(t)

L6: u′(t)=Φ−1(t)f(t)

L7: u(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt

L8: xp(t)=Φ∫Φ−1f(t)dt

EXPLANATION

Let's examine each statement in turn.

  • We first consider line L4. Since Φ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are solutions to the homogeneous system x′(t)=Ax(t), i.e., by substituting any column c(t) of Φ into the homogeneous system, we get c′(t)=Ac(t), where c′(t) is the corresponding column of derivatives in Φ. As a result, this means that Φ′=AΦ. Therefore, L4 follows from the fact that Φ is a fundamental matrix.

  • Next, we consider lines L3, L4, and L5. Let's substitute Φ′=AΦ from L4 into L3: Φu′(t)+Φ′u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)Φu′(t)+AΦu(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)Φu′(t)=f(t) Therefore, L5 follows from L3 and L4 by substitution.

  • Next, we consider lines L6 and L7. To get L7, we are integrating both sides of the equation in L6: ∫u′(t)dt=∫Φ−1(t)f(t)dtu(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt

  • Finally, we consider lines L1, L7, and L8. Substituting u(t)=∫Φ−1f(t)dt from L7 into L1, we get xp(t)=Φu(t)=Φ∫Φ−1f(t)dt. Therefore, L8 is obtained by substituting L7 into L1.

$$

where ${c}^{′}(t)$ is the corresponding column of derivatives in $Φ.$ As a result, this means that ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ.$ Therefore, $\text{L4}$ follows from the fact that $Φ\text{ is a fundamental}$ matrix.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L3}$, $\text{L4},$ and $\text{L5}.$ Let's substitute ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$ from $\text{L4}$ into $\text{L3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)+\cancel{AΦu(t)}=\cancel{AΦu(t)}+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L5}$ follows from $\text{L3}\text{ and }\text{L4}$ by substitution.

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L6}$ and $\text{L7}.$ To get $\text{L7},$ we are $\text{integrating}$ both sides of the equation in $\text{L6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {u}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t & =\int {Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)\,\text{d}t \\ u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L1},$ $\text{L7},$ and $\text{L8}.$ Substituting

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

from $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φu(t) \\  & =Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L8}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L7}$ into $\text{L1}.$

$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ -5 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+\overset{f(t)}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 4{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]}},\,Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{-t} & -3{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations and the fundamental matrix of the corresponding homogeneous system above. Using the method of variation of parameters, compute ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)$ and the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t)$ of the system.
${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} $\,,\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)={e}^{t}\,\,$ {{field-2}}
$\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}$ $\frac{17}{6}$
question.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{-t} & -3{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 4{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{0\cdot (-3{e}^{4t})-3{e}^{4t}\cdot {e}^{-t}}[\begin{aligned}-3{e}^{4t} & -3{e}^{4t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-3t}}{3}[\begin{aligned}-3{e}^{4t} & -3{e}^{4t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-4t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-4t} & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 4{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2t} \\ \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 5{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int \frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 3{e}^{4t} \\ {e}^{-t} & -3{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{t} \\ \frac{17}{6}{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{17}{6}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
