question.html:
Question 13
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=2x3coth⁡x.

a
6x(2tanh⁡x−x2sech2⁡x)
b
6x2(tanh⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
c
2x2(3coth⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
d
2x(2coth⁡x+x2sech2⁡x)
e
2x2(coth⁡x+xcsch2⁡x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=2x3 and v(x)=coth⁡x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(2x3)′⋅coth⁡x+2x3⋅(coth⁡x)′=6x2⋅coth⁡x+2x3⋅(−csch2⁡x)=6x2coth⁡x−2x3csch2⁡x=2x2(3coth⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule

observed_steps.name: Question 14
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule
observed_steps.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=2x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(2x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}+2x\cdot {(\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2})}^{′} \\  & =2\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}+2x\cdot (-2x{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =2\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}-4{x}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2} \\  & =2(\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}-2{x}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 14
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=2x\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=2x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(2x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}+2x\cdot {(\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2})}^{′} \\  & =2\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}+2x\cdot (-2x{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =2\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}-4{x}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2} \\  & =2(\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}-2{x}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=2xcoth⁡x2.

a
2(coth⁡x2+2x2sech2⁡x2)
b
2(coth⁡x2−2x2csch2⁡x2)
c
 2coth⁡x2(1+2x2csch⁡x2)
d
 2coth⁡x2(1−2x2sech⁡x2)
e
2(coth⁡2x−2x2csch2⁡2x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=2x and v(x)=coth⁡x2. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(2x)′⋅coth⁡x2+2x⋅(coth⁡x2)′=2⋅coth⁡x2+2x⋅(−2xcsch2⁡x2)=2coth⁡x2−4x2csch2⁡x2=2(coth⁡x2−2x2csch2⁡x2)

observed_steps.name: Question 15
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule
observed_steps.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡3x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(x)^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sech}⁡3x+x\cdot (\operatorname{sech}⁡3x)^{′} \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{sech}⁡3x+x\cdot (-3\operatorname{sech}⁡3x\cdot \operatorname{tanh}⁡3x) \\  & =\operatorname{sech}⁡3x-3x\operatorname{sech}⁡3x\operatorname{tanh}⁡3x \\  & =\operatorname{sech}⁡3x(1-3x\operatorname{tanh}⁡3x)\end{aligned}
$$

observed_steps.name: Question 16
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule
observed_steps.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{x})}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{\overset{g(x)}{\overset{⏞}{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+1)}}}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+1).$

question.html:
Question 16
?

If f(x)=csch⁡xln⁡x, then f′(x)=−g(x)xln2⁡x. What is g(x)?

a
sech⁡x(ln⁡xcoth⁡x−1)
b
csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1)
c
csch⁡x(coth⁡x+1)
d
sech⁡x(coth⁡x+1)
e
csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=csch⁡x and v(x)=ln⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(csch⁡x)′⋅ln⁡x−csch⁡x⋅(ln⁡x)′(ln⁡x)2=(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)⋅ln⁡x−csch⁡x⋅(1x)ln2⁡x=−csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1)⏞g(x)xln2⁡x

Therefore, g(x)=csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1).

observed_steps.name: Question 17
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule
observed_steps.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)=2{x}^{2}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}\cdot 2{x}^{2}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot (2{x}^{2})^{′}}{(2{x}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x-4x\operatorname{csch}⁡x}{4{x}^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{2x\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+2)}{4{x}^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+2)}{2{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 17
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=csch⁡x2x2.

a
−csch⁡x(coth⁡x−x)2x3
b
−csch⁡x(coth⁡x+x)x3
c
−csch⁡x(xcoth⁡x+2)2x3
d
4csch⁡x(coth⁡x+2)x4
e
csch⁡x(coth⁡x−2x)2x4
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=csch⁡x and v(x)=2x2.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(csch⁡x)′⋅2x2−csch⁡x⋅(2x2)′(2x2)2=−2x2csch⁡xcoth⁡x−4xcsch⁡x4x4=−2xcsch⁡x(xcoth⁡x+2)4x4=−csch⁡x(xcoth⁡x+2)2x3
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule

observed_steps.name: Question 18
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule
observed_steps.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{\overset{g(x)}{\overset{⏞}{\operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}}}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).$

question.html:
Question 18
?

If f(x)=sech⁡xsin⁡x, then f′(x)=−g(x)sin2⁡x. What is g(x)?

a
tanh⁡x(sech⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
b
cosh⁡x(coth⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
c
tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x
d
sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
e
coth⁡xsin⁡x−cos⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=sech⁡x and v(x)=sin⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(sech⁡x)′⋅sin⁡x−sech⁡x⋅(sin⁡x)′(sin⁡x)2=(−sech⁡xtanh⁡x)⋅sin⁡x−sech⁡x⋅(cos⁡x)sin2⁡x=−sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)⏞g(x)sin2⁡x

Therefore, g(x)=sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x).

observed_steps.name: Question 19
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule
observed_steps.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡2x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{({x}^{2})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sech}⁡2x-{x}^{2}\cdot {(\operatorname{sech}⁡2x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{sech}⁡2x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{sech}⁡2x-{x}^{2}(-2\operatorname{sech}⁡2x\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)}{{sech}^{2}⁡2x} \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{sech}⁡2x(1+x\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)}{{sech}^{2}⁡2x} \\  & =\frac{2x(1+x\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)}{\operatorname{sech}⁡2x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Find the derivative of f(x)=x2sech⁡2x.

a
 −2x2tanh2⁡2xsech⁡2x
b
 2x(1−xtanh⁡2x)sech⁡2x
c
 2x(1+xtanh⁡2x)sech⁡2x
d

e
 2x(sech⁡2x−xtanh2⁡2x)sech2⁡2x
Submit

EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=x2 and v(x)=sech⁡2x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(x2)′⋅sech⁡2x−x2⋅(sech⁡2x)′(sech⁡2x)2=2xsech⁡2x−x2(−2sech⁡2xtanh⁡2x)sech2⁡2x=2xsech⁡2x(1+xtanh⁡2x)sech2⁡2x=2x(1+xtanh⁡2x)sech⁡2x

observed_steps.name: Question 20
observed_steps.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule
observed_steps.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)={3}^{x}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot {3}^{x}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot {({3}^{x})}^{′}}{{({3}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x)\cdot {3}^{x}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot ({3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{{3}^{x}\operatorname{csch}⁡x(\operatorname{coth}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(\operatorname{coth}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{x}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 20
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=csch⁡x3x.

a
csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x
b
sech⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
c
−csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x
d
−sech⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
e
−csch⁡x(tanh⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=csch⁡x and v(x)=3x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows: f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(csch⁡x)′⋅3x−csch⁡x⋅(3x)′(3x)2=(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)⋅3x−csch⁡x⋅(3xln⁡3)32x=−3xcsch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x=−csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x

question.name: Question 1
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $y=4\operatorname{coth}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{coth}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =4(-{csch}^{2}⁡x)-(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-4{csch}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{csch}⁡x(-4\operatorname{csch}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 1
?

Find the derivative of y=4coth⁡x−csch⁡x.

a
sech⁡x(4sech⁡x−coth⁡x)
b
csch⁡x(−4csch⁡x+coth⁡x)
c
−csch⁡x(4csch⁡x+coth⁡x)
d
4csch2⁡x−coth⁡x
e
−4csch2⁡x+coth⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(4coth⁡x−csch⁡x)=4ddx(coth⁡x)−ddx(csch⁡x)=4(−csch2⁡x)−(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)=−4csch2⁡x+csch⁡xcoth⁡x=csch⁡x(−4csch⁡x+coth⁡x).

last_observation.name: Question 1
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Basic Derivatives of the Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{coth}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =4(-{csch}^{2}⁡x)-(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-4{csch}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{csch}⁡x(-4\operatorname{csch}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 1
?

Find the derivative of y=4coth⁡x−csch⁡x.

a
sech⁡x(4sech⁡x−coth⁡x)
b
csch⁡x(−4csch⁡x+coth⁡x)
c
−csch⁡x(4csch⁡x+coth⁡x)
d
4csch2⁡x−coth⁡x
e
−4csch2⁡x+coth⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(4coth⁡x−csch⁡x)=4ddx(coth⁡x)−ddx(csch⁡x)=4(−csch2⁡x)−(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)=−4csch2⁡x+csch⁡xcoth⁡x=csch⁡x(−4csch⁡x+coth⁡x).
question.knowledge_point: Basic Derivatives of the Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions

solution.reasoning: Using (coth x)' = -csch² x and (csch x)' = -csch x coth x, y' = -4csch² x + csch x coth x = csch x(-4csch x + coth x), which matches option b. The supplied example supports these derivative rules, but no Math Academy answer or grade for the current question is captured.

feedback.name: Question 1
feedback.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $y=4\operatorname{coth}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\operatorname{coth}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =4(-{csch}^{2}⁡x)-(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-4{csch}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x \\  & =\operatorname{csch}⁡x(-4\operatorname{csch}⁡x+\operatorname{coth}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.html:
Question 1
?

Find the derivative of y=4coth⁡x−csch⁡x.

a
sech⁡x(4sech⁡x−coth⁡x)
b
csch⁡x(−4csch⁡x+coth⁡x)
c
−csch⁡x(4csch⁡x+coth⁡x)
d
4csch2⁡x−coth⁡x
e
−4csch2⁡x+coth⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(4coth⁡x−csch⁡x)=4ddx(coth⁡x)−ddx(csch⁡x)=4(−csch2⁡x)−(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)=−4csch2⁡x+csch⁡xcoth⁡x=csch⁡x(−4csch⁡x+coth⁡x).
feedback.knowledge_point: Example: Basic Derivatives of the Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions

question.name: Question 2
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $y=6\operatorname{coth}⁡x.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =6\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =6(-{csch}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =-6{csch}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.name: Question 2
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Basic Derivatives of the Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =6\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =6(-{csch}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =-6{csch}^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 2
?

Find the derivative of y=6coth⁡x.

a
 −6csch2⁡x
b
 6sech⁡xcoth⁡x
c
−6sech2⁡x
d
 −6csch⁡xtanh⁡x
e
 6csch2⁡x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(6coth⁡x)=6ddx(coth⁡x)=6(−csch2⁡x)=−6csch2⁡x.

Question 2
?

Find the derivative of y=6coth⁡x.

a
 −6csch2⁡x
b
 6sech⁡xcoth⁡x
c
−6sech2⁡x
d
 −6csch⁡xtanh⁡x
e
 6csch2⁡x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(6coth⁡x)=6ddx(coth⁡x)=6(−csch2⁡x)=−6csch2⁡x.

question.name: Question 3
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $y=-3\operatorname{csch}⁡x.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-3\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =-3(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =3\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 3
?

Find the derivative of y=−3csch⁡x.

a
 −3csch2⁡x
b
 3sech⁡xtanh⁡x
c
 3sech⁡x
d
 3csch⁡xcoth⁡x
e
 −3csch⁡xcoth⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(−3csch⁡x)=−3ddx(csch⁡x)=−3(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)=3csch⁡xcoth⁡x.

question.html:
Question 4
?

Find the derivative of y=3csch⁡x−coth⁡x.

a
csch⁡x(3csch⁡x+coth⁡x)
b
3csch⁡xcoth⁡x−sech2⁡x
c
coth⁡x(csch⁡x−3coth⁡x)
d
csch⁡xcoth⁡x+3csch2⁡x
e
csch⁡x(csch⁡x−3coth⁡x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(3csch⁡x−coth⁡x)=3ddx(csch⁡x)−ddx(coth⁡x)=−3csch⁡xcoth⁡x−(−csch2⁡x)=csch⁡x(csch⁡x−3coth⁡x).

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Basic Derivatives of the Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{csch}⁡x-\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-3\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x-(-{csch}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =\operatorname{csch}⁡x(\operatorname{csch}⁡x-3\operatorname{coth}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 4
?

Find the derivative of y=3csch⁡x−coth⁡x.

a
csch⁡x(3csch⁡x+coth⁡x)
b
3csch⁡xcoth⁡x−sech2⁡x
c
coth⁡x(csch⁡x−3coth⁡x)
d
csch⁡xcoth⁡x+3csch2⁡x
e
csch⁡x(csch⁡x−3coth⁡x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(3csch⁡x−coth⁡x)=3ddx(csch⁡x)−ddx(coth⁡x)=−3csch⁡xcoth⁡x−(−csch2⁡x)=csch⁡x(csch⁡x−3coth⁡x).

solution.reasoning: Using (csch x)' = -csch x coth x and (coth x)' = -csch² x gives y' = -3csch x coth x + csch² x = csch x(csch x - 3coth x), matching option e. The supplied example supports these derivative rules, but no Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

Question 4

Find the derivative of y=3csch⁡x−coth⁡x.

a
csch⁡x(3csch⁡x+coth⁡x)
b
3csch⁡xcoth⁡x−sech2⁡x
c
coth⁡x(csch⁡x−3coth⁡x)
d
csch⁡xcoth⁡x+3csch2⁡x
e
csch⁡x(csch⁡x−3coth⁡x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(3csch⁡x−coth⁡x)=3ddx(csch⁡x)−ddx(coth⁡x)=−3csch⁡xcoth⁡x−(−csch2⁡x)=csch⁡x(csch⁡x−3coth⁡x).

question.name: Question 5
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $y=\operatorname{sech}⁡x-2\operatorname{csch}⁡x.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sech}⁡x-2\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x-2(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x+2\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 5
?

Find the derivative of y=sech⁡x−2csch⁡x.

a
 sech⁡x(tanh⁡x+2csch⁡x)
b
sech⁡x(−tanh⁡x−2sech⁡x)
c
−sech⁡xtanh⁡x+2csch⁡xcoth⁡x
d
−sech⁡xtanh⁡x+2csch2⁡xcoth⁡x
e
sech⁡xtanh⁡x−2csch2⁡xcoth⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(sech⁡x−2csch⁡x)=ddx(sech⁡x)−2ddx(csch⁡x)=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x−2(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x+2csch⁡xcoth⁡x.

last_observation.name: Question 5
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Basic Derivatives of the Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sech}⁡x-2\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x-2(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x+2\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 5
?

Find the derivative of y=sech⁡x−2csch⁡x.

a
 sech⁡x(tanh⁡x+2csch⁡x)
b
sech⁡x(−tanh⁡x−2sech⁡x)
c
−sech⁡xtanh⁡x+2csch⁡xcoth⁡x
d
−sech⁡xtanh⁡x+2csch2⁡xcoth⁡x
e
sech⁡xtanh⁡x−2csch2⁡xcoth⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

(sech⁡x)′=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x,(csch⁡x)′=−csch⁡xcoth⁡x,(coth⁡x)′=−csch2⁡x

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

dydx=ddx(sech⁡x−2csch⁡x)=ddx(sech⁡x)−2ddx(csch⁡x)=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x−2(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x+2csch⁡xcoth⁡x.

solution.reasoning: Using (sech x)' = -sech x tanh x and (csch x)' = -csch x coth x gives y' = -sech x tanh x + 2csch x coth x, matching option c. The supplied example supports these rules, but no Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

feedback.name: Question 5
feedback.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $y=\operatorname{sech}⁡x-2\operatorname{csch}⁡x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we recall the results for the derivatives of the basic reciprocal hyperbolic functions:

$$
(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}=-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x,\,(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)^{′}=-{csch}^{2}⁡x
$$

Differentiating the given function using these results, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sech}⁡x-2\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{csch}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x-2(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x+2\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 6
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=4\operatorname{sech}⁡3x.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=4\operatorname{sech}⁡g,\,g=3x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=-4\operatorname{sech}⁡g\operatorname{tanh}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=3.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =-4\operatorname{sech}⁡g\operatorname{tanh}⁡g\cdot 3 \\  & =-12\operatorname{sech}⁡g\operatorname{tanh}⁡g \\  & =-12\operatorname{sech}⁡3x\operatorname{tanh}⁡3x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 6
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=4sech⁡3x.

a
 8sech⁡3xtanh⁡3x
b
 12csch⁡3xtanh⁡3x
c
 −12sech⁡3xtanh⁡3x
d
 −12tanh2⁡3x
e
 −4csch2⁡3x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=4sech⁡g,g=3x

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=−4sech⁡gtanh⁡g,

and

dgdx=3.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=−4sech⁡gtanh⁡g⋅3=−12sech⁡gtanh⁡g=−12sech⁡3xtanh⁡3x.

First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=4\operatorname{sech}⁡g,\,g=3x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=-4\operatorname{sech}⁡g\operatorname{tanh}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=3.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =-4\operatorname{sech}⁡g\operatorname{tanh}⁡g\cdot 3 \\  & =-12\operatorname{sech}⁡g\operatorname{tanh}⁡g \\  & =-12\operatorname{sech}⁡3x\operatorname{tanh}⁡3x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 6
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=4sech⁡3x.

a
 8sech⁡3xtanh⁡3x
b
 12csch⁡3xtanh⁡3x
c
 −12sech⁡3xtanh⁡3x
d
 −12tanh2⁡3x
e
 −4csch2⁡3x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=4sech⁡g,g=3x

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=−4sech⁡gtanh⁡g,

and

dgdx=3.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=−4sech⁡gtanh⁡g⋅3=−12sech⁡gtanh⁡g=−12sech⁡3xtanh⁡3x.
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule

solution.reasoning: Since (sech u)' = -sech u tanh u and (3x)' = 3, the chain rule gives f'(x) = 4[-sech(3x)tanh(3x)]·3 = -12sech(3x)tanh(3x), matching option c. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

feedback.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=4\operatorname{sech}⁡3x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=4\operatorname{sech}⁡g,\,g=3x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=-4\operatorname{sech}⁡g\operatorname{tanh}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=3.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =-4\operatorname{sech}⁡g\operatorname{tanh}⁡g\cdot 3 \\  & =-12\operatorname{sech}⁡g\operatorname{tanh}⁡g \\  & =-12\operatorname{sech}⁡3x\operatorname{tanh}⁡3x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 7
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=-\operatorname{csch}⁡{x}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=-\operatorname{csch}⁡g,\,g={x}^{2}
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=2x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g\cdot 2x \\  & =2x\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g \\  & =2x\operatorname{csch}⁡{x}^{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 7
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=−csch⁡x2.

a
2xcoth2⁡x2
b
csch⁡2xcoth⁡2x
c
2xcsch⁡x2coth⁡x2
d
−2xsech⁡x2coth⁡x2
e
x2csch⁡x2coth⁡x2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=−csch⁡g,g=x2

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=csch⁡gcoth⁡g,

and

dgdx=2x.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=csch⁡gcoth⁡g⋅2x=2xcsch⁡gcoth⁡g=2xcsch⁡x2coth⁡x2.

question.html:
Question 7
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=−csch⁡x2.

a
2xcoth2⁡x2
b
csch⁡2xcoth⁡2x
c
2xcsch⁡x2coth⁡x2
d
−2xsech⁡x2coth⁡x2
e
x2csch⁡x2coth⁡x2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=−csch⁡g,g=x2

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=csch⁡gcoth⁡g,

and

dgdx=2x.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=csch⁡gcoth⁡g⋅2x=2xcsch⁡gcoth⁡g=2xcsch⁡x2coth⁡x2.
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule

solution.reasoning: The argument of csch is x². Using (csch u)' = -csch u coth u and (x²)' = 2x gives f'(x) = -[-csch(x²)coth(x²)]·2x = 2x csch(x²)coth(x²), matching option c. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

Question 7
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=−csch⁡x2.

a
2xcoth2⁡x2
b
csch⁡2xcoth⁡2x
c
2xcsch⁡x2coth⁡x2
d
−2xsech⁡x2coth⁡x2
e
x2csch⁡x2coth⁡x2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=−csch⁡g,g=x2

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=csch⁡gcoth⁡g,

and

dgdx=2x.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=csch⁡gcoth⁡g⋅2x=2xcsch⁡gcoth⁡g=2xcsch⁡x2coth⁡x2.

question.name: Question 8
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=2{sech}^{2}⁡x.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=2{g}^{2},\,g=\operatorname{sech}⁡x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=4g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =4g(-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x) \\  & =4(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)(-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x) \\  & =-4{sech}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 8
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=2sech2⁡x.

a
 −4sech2⁡xtanh⁡x
b
 4sech⁡xtanh⁡x
c
 4sech⁡xtanh2⁡x
d
2sech⁡x
e
−2sech⁡xtanh2⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=2g2,g=sech⁡x

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=4g,

and

dgdx=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=4g(−sech⁡xtanh⁡x)=4(sech⁡x)(−sech⁡xtanh⁡x)=−4sech2⁡xtanh⁡x.

last_observation.name: Question 8
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=2{g}^{2},\,g=\operatorname{sech}⁡x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=4g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =4g(-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x) \\  & =4(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)(-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x) \\  & =-4{sech}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 8
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=2sech2⁡x.

a
 −4sech2⁡xtanh⁡x
b
 4sech⁡xtanh⁡x
c
 4sech⁡xtanh2⁡x
d
2sech⁡x
e
−2sech⁡xtanh2⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=2g2,g=sech⁡x

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=4g,

and

dgdx=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=4g(−sech⁡xtanh⁡x)=4(sech⁡x)(−sech⁡xtanh⁡x)=−4sech2⁡xtanh⁡x.
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule

solution.reasoning: Here f(x) = 2(sech x)². Applying the chain rule gives f'(x) = 4sech x(-sech x tanh x) = -4sech² x tanh x, matching option a. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

Question 8
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=2sech2⁡x.

a
 −4sech2⁡xtanh⁡x
b
 4sech⁡xtanh⁡x
c
 4sech⁡xtanh2⁡x
d
2sech⁡x
e
−2sech⁡xtanh2⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=2g2,g=sech⁡x

The chain rule states that

dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have

dfdg=4g,

and

dgdx=−sech⁡xtanh⁡x.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=4g(−sech⁡xtanh⁡x)=4(sech⁡x)(−sech⁡xtanh⁡x)=−4sech2⁡xtanh⁡x.

question.name: Question 9
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=-2\operatorname{csch}⁡(1-4x).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=-2\operatorname{csch}⁡g,\,g=1-4x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=2\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=-4.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =2\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g\cdot (-4) \\  & =-8\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g \\  & =-8\operatorname{csch}⁡(1-4x)\operatorname{coth}⁡(1-4x).\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 9
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=−2csch⁡(1−4x).

a
−8sech⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x)
b
−8csch⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x)
c
4sech⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x)
d
2csch⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x)
e
−4csch⁡(1−4x)tanh⁡(1−4x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=−2csch⁡g,g=1−4x

The chain rule states that dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have dfdg=2csch⁡gcoth⁡g,

and dgdx=−4.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=2csch⁡gcoth⁡g⋅(−4)=−8csch⁡gcoth⁡g=−8csch⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x).

last_observation.name: Question 9
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=-2\operatorname{csch}⁡g,\,g=1-4x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=2\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=-4.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =2\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g\cdot (-4) \\  & =-8\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g \\  & =-8\operatorname{csch}⁡(1-4x)\operatorname{coth}⁡(1-4x).\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 9
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=−2csch⁡(1−4x).

a
−8sech⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x)
b
−8csch⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x)
c
4sech⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x)
d
2csch⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x)
e
−4csch⁡(1−4x)tanh⁡(1−4x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=−2csch⁡g,g=1−4x

The chain rule states that dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have dfdg=2csch⁡gcoth⁡g,

and dgdx=−4.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives

dfdx=2csch⁡gcoth⁡g⋅(−4)=−8csch⁡gcoth⁡g=−8csch⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x).
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule

solution.reasoning: Let u = 1 - 4x, so u' = -4. Using (csch u)' = -csch u coth u, the chain rule gives f'(x) = (-2)(-csch u coth u)(-4) = -8csch(1-4x)coth(1-4x), matching option b. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

feedback.name: Question 9
feedback.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=-2\operatorname{csch}⁡(1-4x).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=-2\operatorname{csch}⁡g,\,g=1-4x
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=2\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=-4.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =2\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g\cdot (-4) \\  & =-8\operatorname{csch}⁡g\operatorname{coth}⁡g \\  & =-8\operatorname{csch}⁡(1-4x)\operatorname{coth}⁡(1-4x).\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express f(x) as a composite function:

f=−2csch⁡g,g=1−4x

The chain rule states that dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have dfdg=2csch⁡gcoth⁡g,

dfdx=2csch⁡gcoth⁡g⋅(−4)=−8csch⁡gcoth⁡g=−8csch⁡(1−4x)coth⁡(1−4x).

question.name: Question 10
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡({x}^{2}-1).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=\operatorname{coth}⁡g,\,g={x}^{2}-1
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=-{csch}^{2}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=2x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =-{csch}^{2}⁡g\cdot 2x \\  & =-2x{csch}^{2}⁡g \\  & =-2x{csch}^{2}⁡({x}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.name: Question 10
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule
last_observation.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=\operatorname{coth}⁡g,\,g={x}^{2}-1
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=-{csch}^{2}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=2x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =-{csch}^{2}⁡g\cdot 2x \\  & =-2x{csch}^{2}⁡g \\  & =-2x{csch}^{2}⁡({x}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 10
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=coth⁡(x2−1).

a
−x3csch2⁡2x
b
−2xcsch⁡(x2−1)coth⁡(x2−1)
c
−xcsch2⁡2x
d
−2xcsch2⁡(x2−1)
e
2xsech2⁡(x2−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express f(x) as a composite function: f=coth⁡g,g=x2−1

The chain rule states that dfdx=dfdg⋅dgdx.

Differentiating, we have dfdg=−csch2⁡g,

and dgdx=2x.

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for g gives dfdx=−csch2⁡g⋅2x=−2xcsch2⁡g=−2xcsch2⁡(x2−1).
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Chain Rule

solution.reasoning: Let u = x² - 1, so u' = 2x. Since (coth u)' = -csch² u, the chain rule gives f'(x) = -2x csch²(x² - 1), matching option d. The supplied example supports this rule, but no Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

feedback.name: Question 10
feedback.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡({x}^{2}-1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function:

$$
f=\operatorname{coth}⁡g,\,g={x}^{2}-1
$$

The chain rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}\cdot \frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}g}=-{csch}^{2}⁡g,
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}g}{\text{d}x}=2x.
$$

Finally, multiplying the two results together and substituting for $g$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =-{csch}^{2}⁡g\cdot 2x \\  & =-2x{csch}^{2}⁡g \\  & =-2x{csch}^{2}⁡({x}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 11
question.problem:
$$

If $f(x)={x}^{2}\operatorname{csch}⁡4x,$ then ${f}^{′}(x)=2x\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\cdot g(x).$ What is $g(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡4x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={({x}^{2})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{csch}⁡4x+{x}^{2}\cdot {(\operatorname{csch}⁡4x)}^{′} \\  & =2x\cdot \operatorname{csch}⁡4x+{x}^{2}\cdot (-4\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x) \\  & =2x\operatorname{csch}⁡4x-4{x}^{2}\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x \\  & =2x\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\cdot {{(1-2x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x)}_{⏟}}_{g(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=1-2x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x.$

question.html:
Question 11
?

If f(x)=x2csch⁡4x, then f′(x)=2xcsch⁡4x⋅g(x). What is g(x)?

a
 1+xcoth⁡4x
b
2−xcoth⁡4x
c
1−2xtanh⁡4x
d
 1−2xcoth⁡4x
e
 2+xcsch⁡4x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=x2 and v(x)=csch⁡4x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(x2)′⋅csch⁡4x+x2⋅(csch⁡4x)′=2x⋅csch⁡4x+x2⋅(−4csch⁡4xcoth⁡4x)=2xcsch⁡4x−4x2csch⁡4xcoth⁡4x=2xcsch⁡4x⋅(1−2xcoth⁡4x)⏟g(x)

Therefore, g(x)=1−2xcoth⁡4x.

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={({x}^{2})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{csch}⁡4x+{x}^{2}\cdot {(\operatorname{csch}⁡4x)}^{′} \\  & =2x\cdot \operatorname{csch}⁡4x+{x}^{2}\cdot (-4\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x) \\  & =2x\operatorname{csch}⁡4x-4{x}^{2}\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x \\  & =2x\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\cdot {{(1-2x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x)}_{⏟}}_{g(x)}\end{aligned}

question.html:
Question 11
?

If f(x)=x2csch⁡4x, then f′(x)=2xcsch⁡4x⋅g(x). What is g(x)?

a
 1+xcoth⁡4x
b
2−xcoth⁡4x
c
1−2xtanh⁡4x
d
 1−2xcoth⁡4x
e
 2+xcsch⁡4x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=x2 and v(x)=csch⁡4x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(x2)′⋅csch⁡4x+x2⋅(csch⁡4x)′=2x⋅csch⁡4x+x2⋅(−4csch⁡4xcoth⁡4x)=2xcsch⁡4x−4x2csch⁡4xcoth⁡4x=2xcsch⁡4x⋅(1−2xcoth⁡4x)⏟g(x)

Therefore, g(x)=1−2xcoth⁡4x.
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule

solution.reasoning: The product and chain rules give f'(x) = 2x csch(4x) - 4x² csch(4x)coth(4x) = 2x csch(4x)[1 - 2x coth(4x)]. Thus g(x) = 1 - 2x coth(4x), matching option d. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

feedback.name: Question 11
feedback.problem:
$$

If $f(x)={x}^{2}\operatorname{csch}⁡4x,$ then ${f}^{′}(x)=2x\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\cdot g(x).$ What is $g(x)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡4x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={({x}^{2})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{csch}⁡4x+{x}^{2}\cdot {(\operatorname{csch}⁡4x)}^{′} \\  & =2x\cdot \operatorname{csch}⁡4x+{x}^{2}\cdot (-4\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x) \\  & =2x\operatorname{csch}⁡4x-4{x}^{2}\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x \\  & =2x\operatorname{csch}⁡4x\cdot {{(1-2x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x)}_{⏟}}_{g(x)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=1-2x\operatorname{coth}⁡4x.$

question.name: Question 12
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=-3x{csch}^{2}⁡x.$
question.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=-3x$ and $v(x)={csch}^{2}⁡x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(-3x)}^{′}\cdot {csch}^{2}⁡x+(-3x)\cdot {({csch}^{2}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =-3\cdot {csch}^{2}⁡x-3x\cdot (2\operatorname{csch}⁡x)\cdot (-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-3{csch}^{2}⁡x+6x{csch}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x \\  & =3{csch}^{2}⁡x(2x\operatorname{coth}⁡x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=−3xcsch2⁡x.

a
3csch2⁡x(2xcoth⁡x−1)
b
−3csch2⁡x(2xcoth⁡x+1)
c
3csch⁡x(2xcoth2⁡x−1)
d
−3csch2⁡x(2xcoth2⁡x+1)
e
−3csch⁡x(csch⁡x+2xcoth2⁡x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=−3x and v(x)=csch2⁡x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(−3x)′⋅csch2⁡x+(−3x)⋅(csch2⁡x)′=−3⋅csch2⁡x−3x⋅(2csch⁡x)⋅(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)=−3csch2⁡x+6xcsch2⁡xcoth⁡x=3csch2⁡x(2xcoth⁡x−1)

last_observation.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=-3x$ and $v(x)={csch}^{2}⁡x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(-3x)}^{′}\cdot {csch}^{2}⁡x+(-3x)\cdot {({csch}^{2}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =-3\cdot {csch}^{2}⁡x-3x\cdot (2\operatorname{csch}⁡x)\cdot (-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x) \\  & =-3{csch}^{2}⁡x+6x{csch}^{2}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x \\  & =3{csch}^{2}⁡x(2x\operatorname{coth}⁡x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=−3xcsch2⁡x.

a
3csch2⁡x(2xcoth⁡x−1)
b
−3csch2⁡x(2xcoth⁡x+1)
c
3csch⁡x(2xcoth2⁡x−1)
d
−3csch2⁡x(2xcoth2⁡x+1)
e
−3csch⁡x(csch⁡x+2xcoth2⁡x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=−3x and v(x)=csch2⁡x. So, we apply the product rule:

question.name: Question 13
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=2{x}^{3}\operatorname{coth}⁡x.$
question.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=2{x}^{3}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(2{x}^{3})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡x+2{x}^{3}\cdot {(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =6{x}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡x+2{x}^{3}\cdot (-{csch}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =6{x}^{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡x-2{x}^{3}{csch}^{2}⁡x \\  & =2{x}^{2}(3\operatorname{coth}⁡x-x{csch}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 13
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=2x3coth⁡x.

a
6x(2tanh⁡x−x2sech2⁡x)
b
6x2(tanh⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
c
2x2(3coth⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
d
2x(2coth⁡x+x2sech2⁡x)
e
2x2(coth⁡x+xcsch2⁡x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=2x3 and v(x)=coth⁡x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(2x3)′⋅coth⁡x+2x3⋅(coth⁡x)′=6x2⋅coth⁡x+2x3⋅(−csch2⁡x)=6x2coth⁡x−2x3csch2⁡x=2x2(3coth⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)

last_observation.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=2{x}^{3}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(2{x}^{3})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡x+2{x}^{3}\cdot {(\operatorname{coth}⁡x)}^{′} \\  & =6{x}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡x+2{x}^{3}\cdot (-{csch}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =6{x}^{2}\operatorname{coth}⁡x-2{x}^{3}{csch}^{2}⁡x \\  & =2{x}^{2}(3\operatorname{coth}⁡x-x{csch}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 13
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=2x3coth⁡x.

a
6x(2tanh⁡x−x2sech2⁡x)
b
6x2(tanh⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
c
2x2(3coth⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
d
2x(2coth⁡x+x2sech2⁡x)
e
2x2(coth⁡x+xcsch2⁡x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=2x3 and v(x)=coth⁡x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(2x3)′⋅coth⁡x+2x3⋅(coth⁡x)′=6x2⋅coth⁡x+2x3⋅(−csch2⁡x)=6x2coth⁡x−2x3csch2⁡x=2x2(3coth⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule

solution.reasoning: Using the product rule and (coth x)' = -csch² x gives f'(x) = 6x² coth x - 2x³ csch² x = 2x²(3coth x - x csch² x), matching option c. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

Question 13
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=2x3coth⁡x.

a
6x(2tanh⁡x−x2sech2⁡x)
b
6x2(tanh⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
c
2x2(3coth⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
d
2x(2coth⁡x+x2sech2⁡x)
e
2x2(coth⁡x+xcsch2⁡x)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=2x3 and v(x)=coth⁡x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(2x3)′⋅coth⁡x+2x3⋅(coth⁡x)′=6x2⋅coth⁡x+2x3⋅(−csch2⁡x)=6x2coth⁡x−2x3csch2⁡x=2x2(3coth⁡x−xcsch2⁡x)
feedback.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule

question.name: Question 14
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=2x\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=2x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(2x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}+2x\cdot {(\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2})}^{′} \\  & =2\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}+2x\cdot (-2x{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =2\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}-4{x}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2} \\  & =2(\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}-2{x}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=2xcoth⁡x2.

a
2(coth⁡x2+2x2sech2⁡x2)
b
2(coth⁡x2−2x2csch2⁡x2)
c
 2coth⁡x2(1+2x2csch⁡x2)
d
 2coth⁡x2(1−2x2sech⁡x2)
e
2(coth⁡2x−2x2csch2⁡2x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=2x and v(x)=coth⁡x2. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(2x)′⋅coth⁡x2+2x⋅(coth⁡x2)′=2⋅coth⁡x2+2x⋅(−2xcsch2⁡x2)=2coth⁡x2−4x2csch2⁡x2=2(coth⁡x2−2x2csch2⁡x2)

last_observation.name: Question 14
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule
last_observation.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=2x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(2x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}+2x\cdot {(\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2})}^{′} \\  & =2\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}+2x\cdot (-2x{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =2\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}-4{x}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2} \\  & =2(\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}-2{x}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 14
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=2xcoth⁡x2.

a
2(coth⁡x2+2x2sech2⁡x2)
b
2(coth⁡x2−2x2csch2⁡x2)
c
 2coth⁡x2(1+2x2csch⁡x2)
d
 2coth⁡x2(1−2x2sech⁡x2)
e
2(coth⁡2x−2x2csch2⁡2x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=2x and v(x)=coth⁡x2. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(2x)′⋅coth⁡x2+2x⋅(coth⁡x2)′=2⋅coth⁡x2+2x⋅(−2xcsch2⁡x2)=2coth⁡x2−4x2csch2⁡x2=2(coth⁡x2−2x2csch2⁡x2)
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule

solution.reasoning: The product and chain rules give f'(x) = 2coth(x²) + 2x[-csch²(x²)·2x] = 2[coth(x²) - 2x²csch²(x²)], matching option b. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

feedback.name: Question 14
feedback.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=2x\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=2x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={(2x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}+2x\cdot {(\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2})}^{′} \\  & =2\cdot \operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}+2x\cdot (-2x{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2}) \\  & =2\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}-4{x}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2} \\  & =2(\operatorname{coth}⁡{x}^{2}-2{x}^{2}{csch}^{2}⁡{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 15
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=x\operatorname{sech}⁡3x.$
question.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡3x.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(x)^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sech}⁡3x+x\cdot (\operatorname{sech}⁡3x)^{′} \\  & =1\cdot \operatorname{sech}⁡3x+x\cdot (-3\operatorname{sech}⁡3x\cdot \operatorname{tanh}⁡3x) \\  & =\operatorname{sech}⁡3x-3x\operatorname{sech}⁡3x\operatorname{tanh}⁡3x \\  & =\operatorname{sech}⁡3x(1-3x\operatorname{tanh}⁡3x)\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 15
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=xsech⁡3x.

a
sech⁡x(1+3xtanh⁡x)
b
sech⁡3x+tanh⁡3x
c
1+sech⁡x+3xtan⁡x
d
3sech⁡x(1+tanh⁡3x)
e
sech⁡3x(1−3xtanh⁡3x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=x and v(x)=sech⁡3x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(x)′⋅sech⁡3x+x⋅(sech⁡3x)′=1⋅sech⁡3x+x⋅(−3sech⁡3x⋅tanh⁡3x)=sech⁡3x−3xsech⁡3xtanh⁡3x=sech⁡3x(1−3xtanh⁡3x)

question.html:
Question 15
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=xsech⁡3x.

a
sech⁡x(1+3xtanh⁡x)
b
sech⁡3x+tanh⁡3x
c
1+sech⁡x+3xtan⁡x
d
3sech⁡x(1+tanh⁡3x)
e
sech⁡3x(1−3xtanh⁡3x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=x and v(x)=sech⁡3x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(x)′⋅sech⁡3x+x⋅(sech⁡3x)′=1⋅sech⁡3x+x⋅(−3sech⁡3x⋅tanh⁡3x)=sech⁡3x−3xsech⁡3xtanh⁡3x=sech⁡3x(1−3xtanh⁡3x)
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule

solution.reasoning: The product and chain rules give f'(x) = sech(3x) - 3x sech(3x)tanh(3x) = sech(3x)[1 - 3x tanh(3x)], matching option e. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

Question 15
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=xsech⁡3x.

a
sech⁡x(1+3xtanh⁡x)
b
sech⁡3x+tanh⁡3x
c
1+sech⁡x+3xtan⁡x
d
3sech⁡x(1+tanh⁡3x)
e
sech⁡3x(1−3xtanh⁡3x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Here, we have the product of two functions u(x)=x and v(x)=sech⁡3x. So, we apply the product rule:

f′(x)=(x)′⋅sech⁡3x+x⋅(sech⁡3x)′=1⋅sech⁡3x+x⋅(−3sech⁡3x⋅tanh⁡3x)=sech⁡3x−3xsech⁡3xtanh⁡3x=sech⁡3x(1−3xtanh⁡3x)
feedback.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Product Rule

question.name: Question 16
question.problem:
$$

If $f(x)=\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x},$ then ${f}^{′}(x)=-\frac{g(x)}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}.$ What is $g(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{x})}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{\overset{g(x)}{\overset{⏞}{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+1)}}}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+1).$

question.html:
Question 16
?

If f(x)=csch⁡xln⁡x, then f′(x)=−g(x)xln2⁡x. What is g(x)?

a
sech⁡x(ln⁡xcoth⁡x−1)
b
csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1)
c
csch⁡x(coth⁡x+1)
d
sech⁡x(coth⁡x+1)
e
csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=csch⁡x and v(x)=ln⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(csch⁡x)′⋅ln⁡x−csch⁡x⋅(ln⁡x)′(ln⁡x)2=(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)⋅ln⁡x−csch⁡x⋅(1x)ln2⁡x=−csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1)⏞g(x)xln2⁡x

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule
last_observation.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{x})}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{\overset{g(x)}{\overset{⏞}{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+1)}}}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+1).$

question.html:
Question 16
?

If f(x)=csch⁡xln⁡x, then f′(x)=−g(x)xln2⁡x. What is g(x)?

a
sech⁡x(ln⁡xcoth⁡x−1)
b
csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1)
c
csch⁡x(coth⁡x+1)
d
sech⁡x(coth⁡x+1)
e
csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=csch⁡x and v(x)=ln⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(csch⁡x)′⋅ln⁡x−csch⁡x⋅(ln⁡x)′(ln⁡x)2=(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)⋅ln⁡x−csch⁡x⋅(1x)ln2⁡x=−csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1)⏞g(x)xln2⁡x

Therefore, g(x)=csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1).
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule

solution.reasoning: The quotient rule gives f'(x) = [-csch x coth x ln x - csch x/x]/(ln x)² = -csch x[x ln x coth x + 1]/[x(ln x)²]. Thus g(x) matches option b. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

feedback.name: Question 16
feedback.problem:
$$

If $f(x)=\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x},$ then ${f}^{′}(x)=-\frac{g(x)}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}.$ What is $g(x)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{x})}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{\overset{g(x)}{\overset{⏞}{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+1)}}}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+1).$

Question 16
?

If f(x)=csch⁡xln⁡x, then f′(x)=−g(x)xln2⁡x. What is g(x)?

a
sech⁡x(ln⁡xcoth⁡x−1)
b
csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1)
c
csch⁡x(coth⁡x+1)
d
sech⁡x(coth⁡x+1)
e
csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=csch⁡x and v(x)=ln⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(csch⁡x)′⋅ln⁡x−csch⁡x⋅(ln⁡x)′(ln⁡x)2=(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)⋅ln⁡x−csch⁡x⋅(1x)ln2⁡x=−csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1)⏞g(x)xln2⁡x

Therefore, g(x)=csch⁡x(xln⁡xcoth⁡x+1).

question.name: Question 17
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}.$
question.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)=2{x}^{2}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}\cdot 2{x}^{2}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot (2{x}^{2})^{′}}{(2{x}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x-4x\operatorname{csch}⁡x}{4{x}^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{2x\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+2)}{4{x}^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+2)}{2{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.name: Question 17
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule
last_observation.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)=2{x}^{2}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}\cdot 2{x}^{2}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot (2{x}^{2})^{′}}{(2{x}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x-4x\operatorname{csch}⁡x}{4{x}^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{2x\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+2)}{4{x}^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+2)}{2{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$

question.html:
Question 17
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=csch⁡x2x2.

a
−csch⁡x(coth⁡x−x)2x3
b
−csch⁡x(coth⁡x+x)x3
c
−csch⁡x(xcoth⁡x+2)2x3
d
4csch⁡x(coth⁡x+2)x4
e
csch⁡x(coth⁡x−2x)2x4
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=csch⁡x and v(x)=2x2.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(csch⁡x)′⋅2x2−csch⁡x⋅(2x2)′(2x2)2=−2x2csch⁡xcoth⁡x−4xcsch⁡x4x4=−2xcsch⁡x(xcoth⁡x+2)4x4=−csch⁡x(xcoth⁡x+2)2x3
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule

solution.reasoning: The quotient rule gives f'(x) = [(-csch x coth x)(2x²) - (csch x)(4x)]/(4x⁴) = -csch x(x coth x + 2)/(2x³), matching option c. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

feedback.name: Question 17
feedback.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x}{2{x}^{2}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)=2{x}^{2}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)^{′}\cdot 2{x}^{2}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot (2{x}^{2})^{′}}{(2{x}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-2{x}^{2}\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x-4x\operatorname{csch}⁡x}{4{x}^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{2x\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+2)}{4{x}^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(x\operatorname{coth}⁡x+2)}{2{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 18
question.problem:
$$

If $f(x)=\frac{\operatorname{sech}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ then ${f}^{′}(x)=-\frac{g(x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}.$ What is $g(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{\overset{g(x)}{\overset{⏞}{\operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}}}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).$

Question 18
?

If f(x)=sech⁡xsin⁡x, then f′(x)=−g(x)sin2⁡x. What is g(x)?

a
tanh⁡x(sech⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
b
cosh⁡x(coth⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
c
tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x
d
sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
e
coth⁡xsin⁡x−cos⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=sech⁡x and v(x)=sin⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(sech⁡x)′⋅sin⁡x−sech⁡x⋅(sin⁡x)′(sin⁡x)2=(−sech⁡xtanh⁡x)⋅sin⁡x−sech⁡x⋅(cos⁡x)sin2⁡x=−sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)⏞g(x)sin2⁡x

Therefore, g(x)=sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x).

last_observation.name: Question 18
last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule
last_observation.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{\overset{g(x)}{\overset{⏞}{\operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}}}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).$

question.html:
Question 18
?

If f(x)=sech⁡xsin⁡x, then f′(x)=−g(x)sin2⁡x. What is g(x)?

a
tanh⁡x(sech⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
b
cosh⁡x(coth⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
c
tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x
d
sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
e
coth⁡xsin⁡x−cos⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=sech⁡x and v(x)=sin⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(sech⁡x)′⋅sin⁡x−sech⁡x⋅(sin⁡x)′(sin⁡x)2=(−sech⁡xtanh⁡x)⋅sin⁡x−sech⁡x⋅(cos⁡x)sin2⁡x=−sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)⏞g(x)sin2⁡x

Therefore, g(x)=sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x).
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule

solution.reasoning: The quotient rule gives f'(x) = [-sech x tanh x sin x - sech x cos x]/sin² x = -sech x(tanh x sin x + cos x)/sin² x. Thus g(x) matches option d. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

feedback.name: Question 18
feedback.problem:
$$

If $f(x)=\frac{\operatorname{sech}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ then ${f}^{′}(x)=-\frac{g(x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}.$ What is $g(x)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{sech}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot {(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\operatorname{tanh}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sech}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{\overset{g(x)}{\overset{⏞}{\operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)}}}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡x(\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).$

feedback.html:
Question 18
?

If f(x)=sech⁡xsin⁡x, then f′(x)=−g(x)sin2⁡x. What is g(x)?

a
tanh⁡x(sech⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
b
cosh⁡x(coth⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
c
tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x
d
sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)
e
coth⁡xsin⁡x−cos⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=sech⁡x and v(x)=sin⁡x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(sech⁡x)′⋅sin⁡x−sech⁡x⋅(sin⁡x)′(sin⁡x)2=(−sech⁡xtanh⁡x)⋅sin⁡x−sech⁡x⋅(cos⁡x)sin2⁡x=−sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x)⏞g(x)sin2⁡x

Therefore, g(x)=sech⁡x(tanh⁡xsin⁡x+cos⁡x).

question.name: Question 19
question.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{\operatorname{sech}⁡2x}.$
question.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡2x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{({x}^{2})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sech}⁡2x-{x}^{2}\cdot {(\operatorname{sech}⁡2x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{sech}⁡2x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{sech}⁡2x-{x}^{2}(-2\operatorname{sech}⁡2x\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)}{{sech}^{2}⁡2x} \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{sech}⁡2x(1+x\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)}{{sech}^{2}⁡2x} \\  & =\frac{2x(1+x\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)}{\operatorname{sech}⁡2x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 19
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=x2sech⁡2x.

a
 −2x2tanh2⁡2xsech⁡2x
b
 2x(1−xtanh⁡2x)sech⁡2x
c
 2x(1+xtanh⁡2x)sech⁡2x
d
 2x(sech⁡2x+xtanh2⁡2x)sech2⁡2x
e
 2x(sech⁡2x−xtanh2⁡2x)sech2⁡2x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=x2 and v(x)=sech⁡2x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(x2)′⋅sech⁡2x−x2⋅(sech⁡2x)′(sech⁡2x)2=2xsech⁡2x−x2(−2sech⁡2xtanh⁡2x)sech2⁡2x=2xsech⁡2x(1+xtanh⁡2x)sech2⁡2x=2x(1+xtanh⁡2x)sech⁡2x

last_observation.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)={x}^{2}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sech}⁡2x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{({x}^{2})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{sech}⁡2x-{x}^{2}\cdot {(\operatorname{sech}⁡2x)}^{′}}{{(\operatorname{sech}⁡2x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{sech}⁡2x-{x}^{2}(-2\operatorname{sech}⁡2x\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)}{{sech}^{2}⁡2x} \\  & =\frac{2x\operatorname{sech}⁡2x(1+x\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)}{{sech}^{2}⁡2x} \\  & =\frac{2x(1+x\operatorname{tanh}⁡2x)}{\operatorname{sech}⁡2x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot {3}^{x}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot {({3}^{x})}^{′}}{{({3}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x)\cdot {3}^{x}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot ({3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{{3}^{x}\operatorname{csch}⁡x(\operatorname{coth}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(\operatorname{coth}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{x}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 20
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=csch⁡x3x.

a
csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x
b
sech⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
c
−csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x
d
−sech⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
e
−csch⁡x(tanh⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=csch⁡x and v(x)=3x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows: f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(csch⁡x)′⋅3x−csch⁡x⋅(3x)′(3x)2=(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)⋅3x−csch⁡x⋅(3xln⁡3)32x=−3xcsch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x=−csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x

last_observation.knowledge_point: Example: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule
last_observation.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)={3}^{x}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot {3}^{x}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot {({3}^{x})}^{′}}{{({3}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x)\cdot {3}^{x}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot ({3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{{3}^{x}\operatorname{csch}⁡x(\operatorname{coth}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(\operatorname{coth}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{x}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 20
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=csch⁡x3x.

a
csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x
b
sech⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
c
−csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x
d
−sech⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
e
−csch⁡x(tanh⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=csch⁡x and v(x)=3x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows: f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(csch⁡x)′⋅3x−csch⁡x⋅(3x)′(3x)2=(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)⋅3x−csch⁡x⋅(3xln⁡3)32x=−3xcsch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x=−csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x
question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions Using the Quotient Rule

solution.reasoning: Using (csch x)' = -csch x coth x and (3^x)' = 3^x ln 3, the quotient rule gives f'(x) = [-3^x csch x coth x - 3^x csch x ln 3]/3^(2x) = -csch x(coth x + ln 3)/3^x, matching option c. No Math Academy answer or grade for this question is captured.

feedback.name: Question 20
feedback.problem:
$$

Find the derivative of $f(x)=\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x}{{3}^{x}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{csch}⁡x$ and $v(x)={3}^{x}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{(\operatorname{csch}⁡x)}^{′}\cdot {3}^{x}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot {({3}^{x})}^{′}}{{({3}^{x})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\operatorname{coth}⁡x)\cdot {3}^{x}-\operatorname{csch}⁡x\cdot ({3}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{{3}^{x}\operatorname{csch}⁡x(\operatorname{coth}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{2x}} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{csch}⁡x(\operatorname{coth}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}{{3}^{x}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.html:
Question 20
?

Find the derivative of f(x)=csch⁡x3x.

a
csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x
b
sech⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
c
−csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x
d
−sech⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
e
−csch⁡x(tanh⁡x+ln⁡3)32x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

In this case, the expression for f(x) is a quotient u(x)v(x) with u(x)=csch⁡x and v(x)=3x.

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows: f′(x)=u′(x)⋅v(x)−u(x)⋅v′(x)[v(x)]2=(csch⁡x)′⋅3x−csch⁡x⋅(3x)′(3x)2=(−csch⁡xcoth⁡x)⋅3x−csch⁡x⋅(3xln⁡3)32x=−3xcsch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)32x=−csch⁡x(coth⁡x+ln⁡3)3x

questions.name: Question 1
questions.problem:
If the midpoint of the line segment with endpoints $(-5,3)$ and $(a,b)$ is $(1,4),$
then $a+b=$
questions.worked_solution:
The given points are ${{(-5,3)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{1},\,{y}_{1})},$ ${{(a,b)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{2},\,{y}_{2})}$ and ${{(1,4)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{m},\,{y}_{m})}\,.$

We use the midpoint formula as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}_{m},{y}_{m}) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\ (1,4) & =(\frac{-5+a}{2},\frac{3+b}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding $x$- and $y$-coordinates in the equation above gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}1=\frac{-5+a}{2} \\ 4=\frac{3+b}{2}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}a=7 \\ b=5.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $(a,b)=(7,5)$ and $a+b=12.$

The midpoint is ((a+5a)/2,(2b+7b)/2)=(3a,9b/2), agreeing with the earlier answer, submitted response, Correct grade, and final worked answer. If the midpoint of the line segment with endpoints $(-5,3)$ and $(a,b)$ is $(1,4),$
then $a+b=$
question.worked_solution:
The given points are ${{(-5,3)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{1},\,{y}_{1})},$ ${{(a,b)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{2},\,{y}_{2})}$ and ${{(1,4)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{m},\,{y}_{m})}\,.$

We use the midpoint formula as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}_{m},{y}_{m}) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\ (1,4) & =(\frac{-5+a}{2},\frac{3+b}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding $x$- and $y$-coordinates in the equation above gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}1=\frac{-5+a}{2} \\ 4=\frac{3+b}{2}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}a=7 \\ b=5.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $(a,b)=(7,5)$ and $a+b=12.$

questions.name: Question 1
questions.problem: If $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}$ and $r(t)={e}^{t}\,i+{e}^{-t}\,j,$ compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$
questions.worked_solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,j \\  & =2x\,i+2y\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={e}^{t}$ and $y={e}^{-t}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =2{e}^{t}\,i+2{e}^{-t}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})\,j \\  & ={e}^{t}\,i-{e}^{-t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =(2{e}^{t}\,i+2{e}^{-t}\,j)\cdot ({e}^{t}\,i-{e}^{-t}\,j) \\  & =2{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{t}-2{e}^{-t}\cdot {e}^{-t} \\  & =2{e}^{2t}-2{e}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}
$$
